title: Accept ADR-029: MIT OR Apache-2.0 dual license
description: ADR-029 is the only ADR still 'Proposed'. Current default: MIT OR Apache-2.0, matching kinemo, hapto and the Rust ecosystem, and compatible with porting Trio tests (MIT/Apache). Decide and change its status to Accepted in 04-decision-records.md before any code lands.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-029 marked Accepted (or revised) in 04-decision-records.md; hk-license unblocked.

title: Release porto and douro 1.0.0
description: Release checklist: all S1-S7 gates and the traceability gate closed, security review closed, ADR index has no 'Proposed' entries, names confirmed (dec-name-collision), changelog built, version bumped to 1.0.0 in lockstep. Tag, publish via the release workflow, update README status and docs version selector, announce with links to published benchmark code.
acceptance_criteria: porto 1.0.0, douro 1.0.0 and porto-console on PyPI with attestations; porto, porto-abi, porto-pyo3 1.0.0 on crates.io; GitHub release with changelog; docs show 1.0.

title: Gate S7: docs cover 100% of the public API with runnable examples
description: Run the doc coverage and doctest checks against the frozen API snapshot; every public porto and douro name has a reference entry and at least one runnable example, and all examples pass.
acceptance_criteria: doc_coverage reports 100% against the m8-api-freeze snapshot; doctest job green on the RC.

title: Gate S6: 72-hour soak clean
description: Run the 72 h soak on the release candidate wheels (GIL build, and 3.14t with lanes=auto) and confirm RSS growth <= 5% after warmup and no FD growth; the nightly leak job is green.
acceptance_criteria: Soak report with RSS/FD series for both builds attached; leak job green on the RC.

title: Gate S5: h2spec and Autobahn pass
description: Confirm the conformance job passes on the release candidate with an empty exceptions file, for TLS h2 and h2c prior knowledge and for WebSockets over h1.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance reports for the RC attached; exceptions file empty.

title: Gate S3: zero known races under TSAN and loom
description: Seven consecutive green nightlies of the exhaustive loom run, Rust TSAN/ASAN and the TSAN-CPython 3.14t suite on the release candidate; zero open race issues; suppression files reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: Links to 7 consecutive green runs of each job; race issue query empty.

title: Gate S4: deterministic reproduction across 1000 reruns
description: On the release candidate, run the deterministic reproduction check for a set of planted bugs (lost wakeup, cancel race, timeout ordering, sim-net partition) and confirm each failing seed reproduces 100% across 1000 reruns with identical traces, on Linux, macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Report with 1000/1000 per planted bug per OS attached to the gate issue.

title: Gate S2: compat suites at >= 95%
description: Confirm asyncpg, redis.asyncio, httpx and aiohttp client suites pass at >= 95% each under porto.run(..., asyncio_compat=True) on the release candidate, on GIL and free-threaded builds, with the expected-failures file reviewed and each entry explained.
acceptance_criteria: Compat job on the RC tag green with per-suite rates >= 95%; expected-failures entries each link an issue or rationale.

title: Gate S1: all benchmark gates pass on the reference machine
description: Run the full §53 suite (micro, free-threaded scaling, HTTP vs all competitors, 1 process and N processes) on the release candidate with PGO wheels. Publish bench/results/<date>-<commit>.json with machine info and the competitor app sources (§53 §5); never publish numbers without the code.
acceptance_criteria: Every §53 gate marked pass in the committed results; results page in the docs links the code and versions.

title: API freeze: Python, Rust and ABI surfaces
description: Review the implemented Python API against §20 and §43 and resolve every difference (code or spec). Snapshot the public surface: porto/douro __all__ and signatures (griffe dump), mypy stubtest of .pyi vs runtime, Rust public API (cargo public-api) for porto/porto-abi/porto-pyo3, and PortoApiV1 layout. CI fails on any unreviewed change to the snapshots. Remove deprecated 0.x aliases.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot files committed; stubtest clean; a signature change fails CI until the snapshot is updated; spec and implementation agree (diff list empty).

title: douro wheel packaging pinned to the porto minor
description: packaging/douro/pyproject.toml: maturin module douro._native from crates/douro-py, python-source with python/douro only, console script douro, dependencies porto>=X.Y,<X.(Y+1) and oxiform (pinned per §34), version kept in lockstep with porto by a check script. CI builds both wheels and installs them together; a test installs a mismatched porto minor and expects the import-time abi_major/version error.
acceptance_criteria: Both wheels install side by side and import; douro console script runs --help; a wrong porto minor yields the clear import error; THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES covers douro-py.

title: Initial CI: lint, rust-test, minimal py-test
description: .github/workflows/ci.yml following kinemo/hapto (push to main, pull_request, workflow_dispatch; concurrency cancel-in-progress; Swatinem/rust-cache). Jobs: lint (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, ruff, pyright --strict), rust-test (cargo nextest on ubuntu-latest, macos-14, windows-latest, --exclude porto-py), py-test minimal (maturin develop + pytest on 3.11 and 3.14, Linux/macOS/Windows). All actions pinned by commit SHA (§40 supply chain), permissions: contents: read. Later milestones add jobs (m*-ci-*).
acceptance_criteria: A PR runs all three jobs green; a formatting error, a clippy warning, a pyright error and a failing pytest each fail the run; the jobs are required checks on main.

title: Dual MIT/Apache-2.0 license files and package metadata
description: Add LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE (same texts and copyright holder as kinemo/hapto), license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0" in [workspace.package] and every packaging/*/pyproject.toml, and license-files listing both plus THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md. README and CONTRIBUTING carry kinemo's inbound=outbound contribution clause.
acceptance_criteria: Both files present; cargo metadata and the built wheel METADATA report MIT OR Apache-2.0; the wheel contains both license files.
notes: From #4: maturin rejects license-files paths with '..'; put LICENSE-MIT/LICENSE-APACHE (copies or symlinks that resolve in the wheel) inside packaging/porto/ and add license-files there; verify both licenses land in the wheel's dist-info.
close_reason: License files merged in #5; wheel and sdist carry both via symlinks in packaging/porto

title: uv workspace and maturin packaging for porto
description: Root pyproject.toml as uv workspace root for dev tooling only (dependency-groups: maturin>=1.x, pytest, pyright, ruff, towncrier, uvloop for baselines). packaging/porto/pyproject.toml builds module porto._core from crates/porto-py with python-source ../../python, version-specific wheels (no abi3, ADR-024), requires-python >=3.11, license-files, Typing :: Typed classifier. python/porto/ gets __init__.py (re-exports, __version__), _core.pyi and py.typed (ADR-028). Placeholders for packaging/douro and packaging/porto-console are added by M6/M5.
acceptance_criteria: uv sync then uv run maturin develop -m packaging/porto/pyproject.toml builds; python -c 'import porto; print(porto.__version__)' works on 3.11 and 3.14; maturin build produces a cp311 (not abi3) wheel containing py.typed and _core.pyi.
close_reason: uv workspace + maturin packaging merged in #4; import works on 3.11, 3.14, 3.14t (GIL stays off)

title: Initialize git repository and GitHub project
description: The porto directory is not yet a git repository. Run git init with main as default branch, add .gitignore (target/, .venv/, dist/, *.so/*.pyd, site/, bench/results/tmp) and .gitattributes (LF, *.pyi diff=python), and commit the spec as the first commit; drop porto-douro-spec.zip from the tree (the spec in docs/spec is the source). Create the GitHub repo (m4nd0r4s/porto, like kinemo/hapto), enable private vulnerability reporting, Discussions and Pages, and protect main (required checks added by hk-ci-baseline, no force-push).
acceptance_criteria: git log shows the spec commit; remote exists; private vulnerability reporting and Discussions are on; main is protected; porto-douro-spec.zip is not tracked.
close_reason: git repo on main with the personal identity, spec in docs/spec, private GitHub repo m4nd0r4s/porto, beads synced to refs/dolt/data

title: Cargo workspace, pinned toolchain, shared lints and profiles
description: Root Cargo.toml workspace (resolver 2, members crates/*) with [workspace.package] (version, edition, license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0", repository, publish = false by default) and [workspace.dependencies] for pyo3 (no abi3, ADR-024). [workspace.lints]: rust unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = deny, missing_docs = warn for public crates; clippy undocumented_unsafe_blocks = deny plus a curated pedantic subset. Profiles: release (lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1, panic = "unwind", opt-level = 3), dist inherits release (PGO hook for M8), dev with line-tables-only like kinemo. rust-toolchain.toml pins one stable version with rustfmt + clippy; rustfmt.toml. Scaffold the crates M0 needs (porto-core, porto-py, porto facade) with lib.rs stubs and the empty top-level dirs from §50 (tests/, bench/micro, bench/http, bench/results, packaging/); later crates are added by the milestone that introduces them.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build --workspace, cargo fmt --all --check and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings pass on a fresh clone; cargo metadata shows the release/dist profile settings; every crate inherits [workspace.lints].
notes: ADR-031: edition 2024, rust-toolchain.toml channel = 1.99.1 (latest stable on 2026-11-04).
close_reason: Cargo workspace merged in #3 (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.1, lints, profiles, porto-core/porto-py/porto)

title: M7 exit: Douro docs complete with runnable examples
description: User docs for every public Douro API with runnable, doc-tested examples: tutorial, routing, params, DI, responses, WS/SSE, middleware/layers, OpenAPI, config/CLI/deployment, testing, limits/security, and the FastAPI -> Douro mapping page.
acceptance_criteria: Doc tests run in CI; coverage script shows 100% of §43 public names documented.

title: M7 exit: graceful-shutdown zero-loss test
description: E2E test sending SIGTERM (and SIGHUP rolling reload) to the supervisor mid-load over h1 and h2, asserting every request either completed or was properly refused (Connection: close / GOAWAY), none lost or reset.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated 50x in CI with zero lost requests on Linux and macOS.

title: douro CLI: run, dev, routes, openapi, config
description: Console script douro: run (host, port, uds, workers N|auto, lanes, tls, http auto|1|2, reload, preload, backlog, graceful-timeout, max-requests, reuse-port, log-level, access-log, config), dev (= run --reload --workers 1 --debug, pretty logs), routes (table with handler locations), openapi (offline export), config explain. --workers auto = physical cores on GIL, 1 on free-threaded.
acceptance_criteria: CLI tests for each subcommand and flag parsing; douro openapi output equals app.openapi().

title: Supervisor: listeners, exec workers, respawn, signals
description: Rust supervisor in douro._native (never starts a Porto runtime): binds TCP/UDS with SO_REUSEADDR, optional SO_REUSEPORT per-worker binds, EPOLLEXCLUSIVE for shared listeners; spawns workers via exec (python -m douro._worker --fd ...); respawn with backoff 1 s -> 30 s, --max-requests with jitter, --max-rss; readiness pipe (exit non-zero if none ready in 60 s); SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful stop, SIGHUP rolling reload, SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU scale.
acceptance_criteria: Process tests for crash respawn backoff, recycling, rolling reload without failed requests, readiness timeout exit code, signal handling.

title: OpenAPI 3.1 generation from plans via OX-5
description: Generate OpenAPI 3.1.0 lazily at first request to openapi_url (None disables), cached as bytes in Rust; schemas from the OX-5 bundle with ref_template #/components/schemas/{name} (validation mode for requests, serialization for responses); operations from method/path/name/tags/docstring, params, bodies, responses incl. responses= map, auto 422 and problem responses, deprecated, include_in_schema; stable operationIds <router>_<handler> or operation_id=; security_schemes + Security markers; app.openapi().
acceptance_criteria: Generated document validates against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema; golden-file tests for a sample app; stable across runs.

title: M7 exit: h2spec conformance in CI
description: Run h2spec against Douro over TLS and h2c prior knowledge; configs under tests/conformance; CI conformance job; fix any deviations.
acceptance_criteria: h2spec passes 100% (TLS and h2c); CI job blocking.

title: M7 exit: Autobahn WebSocket conformance in CI
description: Autobahn testsuite (fuzzingclient) against a Douro echo app incl. permessage-deflate cases; configs under tests/conformance; CI conformance job.
acceptance_criteria: All Autobahn cases OK or NON-STRICT/INFORMATIONAL with documented justification; CI job blocking.

title: douro.WebSocket API and @app.ws routes
description: @app.ws routes with params and dependencies; WebSocket accept(subprotocol), receive/receive_text/receive_bytes/receive_json(type=T) via oxiform, send/send_json, close, ping, async iteration, client_state, headers, query; WebSocketDisconnect(code, reason); dependency validation errors close with 1008. Test client c.websocket() support.
acceptance_criteria: API tests via test client; 1008 on dependency validation failure; receive_json invalid payload raises typed error.

title: WebSocket engine: upgrade, tungstenite sans-io, limits
description: HTTP/1.1 upgrade on the connection stream with tungstenite in sans-io mode: permessage-deflate (negotiated, configurable), fragmentation, ping/pong auto-reply, close handshake with codes; limits max_message_size 1 MiB, max_frame_size, idle_timeout, write high-water mark backpressure. Fuzz target for the frame codec.
acceptance_criteria: Engine-level tests for each feature; frame codec fuzz smoke passes.

title: Python middleware with Rust call_next
description: @app.middleware(fn(request, call_next)) running in the handler's PyTask; call_next is a Rust awaitable running the rest of the chain inline by delegated send (no extra task). Responses pass through Python as douro.Response with lazy body; JSON bytes stay in Rust unless resp.body is read.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: ordering outermost-first, one PyTask per request, short-circuit responses, body stays Rust-side unless read (allocation test).

title: Rust layer pipeline and ordering
description: Layer trait and chain in douro-core: pre-route layers (declaration order) before the router, route-level layers after routing, post-handler path reversed. layers= on App, Router and route compiled into RoutePolicies; layer objects configured from Python classes in douro.layers.
acceptance_criteria: Ordering test matching §35 §2 exactly with recording layers; zero Python crossings for Rust-only chains (crossing counter).

title: M6 exit: HTTP gates on JSON, path-param and POST
description: Run and pass the HTTP gates per process on the GIL build: >= 5x FastAPI+Uvicorn and >= 3x FastAPI+Granian on JSON, path-param and POST-validate; >= 1.0x Granian RSGI on plaintext/JSON; framework tax vs porto raw handler <= 20%; p99 <= 2x p50 at 70% of max RPS. Profile against the §42 per-request budget (target >= 150k req/s/core on path-param model).
acceptance_criteria: Published results file shows all listed gates passing; regressions tracked in CI perf job.

title: douro.testing.Client (memory and tcp transports)
description: Client(app) async context running lifespan; memory transport injects requests at the engine request layer through the full Rust pipeline; tcp transport via a loopback server. httpx-like API (get/post/put/patch/delete/request/stream, json/data/files/headers/cookies, persisted cookie jar, follow_redirects); Response.status/headers/text/content/json()/http_version; .sync() via Portal; honors dependency_overrides; pytest fixture douro_client driven by douro_app.
acceptance_criteria: Douro's own M6 test suite runs on it; same tests pass on memory and tcp transports; sync mode works from a plain pytest function.

title: douro.serve embedding and per-worker graceful shutdown
description: await douro.serve(app, config=ServerConfig, started=porto.Started[int], **overrides) runs inside an existing runtime, plus python -m douro._worker entry for a single process. Graceful shutdown: stop accept, Connection: close on in-flight h1 and close idle, h2 GOAWAY(last_stream_id), wait graceful_timeout (30 s), cancel server scope, exit.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: started reports bound port; shutdown completes in-flight requests and refuses new ones correctly on h1 and h2.

title: HTTPError, exception handlers and problem responses
description: HTTPError(status, detail, title, type_, headers, **extensions) -> application/problem+json; @app.exception_handler matching by MRO after unwrapping single-exception groups from the handler scope (ST-10); unhandled -> 500 problem, traceback only with debug=True, logged with request id.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: MRO matching, group unwrapping, debug on/off bodies, log record contains request id.

title: Rust plan-runner for async and generator deps
description: Rust-implemented runner coroutine awaits Python deps as sub-coroutines by delegated sends inside the handler PyTask (no extra tasks, R2). Generator deps (sync/async): setup before handler, teardown after the response is fully sent, reverse topological order, in a shielded child scope with 10 s deadline; handler exceptions are thrown into the generator.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: one PyTask per request with N deps (task counter), teardown ordering, teardown sees handler exception, teardown runs after last byte written, 10 s deadline enforced.

title: Return value serialization against declared type
description: Map handler returns: None -> 204 (or explicit status), models/dataclasses/TypedDict/containers -> JSON via OX-2 encode against the return annotation (extra subclass fields never written), response_model= and response_model_exclude_none compiled into the serializer, unannotated -> generic ox.json.encode, Response subclasses as-is. Encode into a Rust buffer (OX-6 when available, else copy) so bytes stay in Rust (R4).
acceptance_criteria: Tests for every mapping incl. field filtering of subclass instances; no Python bytes object created on the JSON path (allocation test).

title: DI graph: scopes, cycle detection, overrides
description: Build the dependency graph recursively with the same inference rules; topological sort at freeze; cycle errors show the path. Scopes: request (deduplicated), app (resolved eagerly in lifespan, in parallel where independent, stored in the plan), transient. Rust-known values (Request, Scope, path params) never enter Python. app.dependency_overrides re-freezes affected plans only when not serving or in the test client.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: dedup counts, app-scope evaluated once, transient per use, cycle error text, override applied and rejected while serving.

title: HandlerPlan, AppPlan and vectorcall handler invocation
description: Rust HandlerPlan/ParamPlan/BodyPlan/ResponsePlan/RoutePolicies built from the frozen AppPlan (Arc shared by all lanes). Invoke via PyObject_Vectorcall with a precomputed kwnames tuple (no kwargs dict). HandlerKind: Async (PyTask, no Python Task object), SyncPool (blocking pool, ADR-020), SyncInline (inline=True).
acceptance_criteria: Tests for each HandlerKind; perf test shows no dict allocation per call; sync handler runs off the Python lane by default.

title: Typed body decode via oxiform (strict, by Content-Type)
description: Decode body bytes with the OX-1 body plan in strict mode, format by Content-Type (JSON, *+json, msgpack, yaml), max_bytes = route max_body_size, ox.Limits incl. max_json_depth, context={"request": request}. Support ox.Partial[T] for PATCH and embed-mode bodies keyed by parameter name. Errors merge into the combined 422.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for each format, depth limit, Partial PATCH, embed mode, 422 shape matches oxiform to_problem with body prefix.

title: oxiform plan handles at freeze and re-exports
description: Load the oxiform OX-1 capsule from douro._native; at freeze request plan handles for body, params-models, return and dependency types, call ox.warmup(*types), and surface ox.SchemaError with the handler location prepended. Re-export Model, Email, Url and constraints Ge/Gt/Le/Lt/Len/Pattern/MultipleOf from douro.
acceptance_criteria: Freeze test with forward refs resolves; SchemaError message includes file:line of the handler; douro.Model is ox.Model.

title: Path/query/header/cookie decoding with one combined 422
description: Synthesize one params model per handler and source (aliases, header name x_request_id -> x-request-id, Query(alias=), Query(explode=False)) and decode each source with one OX-3 lax call, including urlencoded Form fields. Accumulate issues across sources and emit one 422 problem via OX-4 with source-prefixed paths.
acceptance_criteria: Coercion tests for every scalar type in §33 §3 incl. lists and Optional; request with errors in path, query and header returns one 422 listing all.

title: Handler signature introspection and source inference
description: _plan.py introspects handlers with get_type_hints(include_extras=True) and inspect.signature and applies inference order: explicit markers (Path, Query, Header, Cookie, Body, Form, File, Depends, State), special types (Request, Response sink, WebSocket, porto.Scope, BodyStream, App, Background), path-name match, structured types -> Body (embed mode for several), else Query. Unannotated parameters fail freeze with the documented message.
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven tests per rule including embed mode and the unannotated error message.

title: App/Router declaration API and freeze phases
description: Python App and Router with get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options/route decorators registering RouteDecl with all route options; include() composing prefixes, tags, deps and inherited options (timeout, on_disconnect, max_body_size, responses, include_in_schema); app.state; freeze() resolving routers and handing an immutable AppPlan to Rust; adding routes after freeze raises RuntimeError.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: option inheritance/override matrix, implicit freeze at first serve/test client, RuntimeError after freeze.

title: Response writer: writev, chunked/DATA, cached headers
description: Fixed bodies with Content-Length written as one coalesced writev; streaming via chunked (h1) or DATA frames (h2) flushed per chunk with socket backpressure; per-lane cached Date header refreshed every second; preencoded common header names; no Server header by default; lane-local buffer pools.
acceptance_criteria: Syscall test shows one write for small fixed responses; Date updates once per second; no Server header in default responses.

title: Body reading, limits, 100-continue, 415/413
description: Read the body into Bytes (zero-copy single-chunk collect) honoring max_body_size and Content-Length precheck (413 without reading); send 100 Continue only when the body is actually read; body_read_idle_timeout; content-type dispatch (json, *+json, urlencoded, octet-stream, text/plain; mismatch -> 415). douro.BodyStream and request.stream() deliver chunks with hyper flow-control backpressure.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for 413 precheck, 100-continue lazy send, 415, idle timeout, BodyStream backpressure under a slow consumer.

title: RequestCtx, request scope and lazy douro.Request
description: Rust RequestHead/RequestCtx (params as ranges, BodyState Unread|Buffered|Consumed, request_id, ScopeHandle as child of the connection scope). douro.Request pyclass over Arc<RequestCtx> created only when asked for, with lazy method, url, path, path_params, query (QueryParams), headers (Headers view, no copy), cookies, client, scheme, http_version, id, state, scope, body(), json(type), stream(), is_disconnected().
acceptance_criteria: Tests for every accessor; allocation test proves no Python objects are created for handlers that do not request Request.

title: HTTP/1.1 connection handling and smuggling defenses
description: hyper-util auto builder with ConnState { peer, tls_info, alpn, requests_served, last_activity }; keep-alive default on, sequential pipelining, max_requests_per_connection, keep_alive_timeout 5 s, header read timeout 10 s. Reject Transfer-Encoding+Content-Length, duplicate Content-Length and obs-fold.
acceptance_criteria: e2e tests for keep-alive, timeouts (header slowloris closes at 10 s under virtual time or short config), smuggling corpus rejected with 400.

title: Accept loop with batching and backpressure
description: Listener created by the worker or inherited by FD; one accept task per lane per listener (free-threaded) or per worker (GIL). accept4 batched up to 64 per readiness event; pause accepting at max_concurrent_requests_per_lane (1024) and resume below 90%; --backlog (2048); TCP_NODELAY on.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: inherited FD works; with a low limit, accept pauses and resumes at the 90% threshold (counter assertions); batched accept verified by syscall counting test.

title: hyper runtime adapters over porto-abi
description: Implement PortoAbiStream (hyper::rt::Read + Write over porto_abi readiness), PortoAbiExecutor (spawn h2 stream tasks via api.spawn into the connection scope) and PortoAbiTimer (sleep_until) in douro-http.
acceptance_criteria: hyper h1 and h2 client/server loopback tests pass using only the ABI; no porto-core symbol linked (checked with nm in CI).

title: Radix router per method with static>param>catch-all
description: Implement douro-router: compressed trie per HTTP method plus an any-method tree; path syntax with {name}, inline types {id:int|str|uuid}, catch-all {p:path} (last only), literal {{ }}. Lookup returns (RouteId, SmallVec<[_;4]> byte ranges) with zero allocation on static paths; deterministic priority static > param > catch-all.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + proptest against a naive matcher; criterion bench shows no allocation on static lookup; priority cases documented and tested.

title: Douro crates, python package and native module skeleton
description: Create crates douro-router, douro-http, douro-core, douro-py (cdylib douro._native) and python/douro with maturin packaging. douro._native links porto-abi (not porto-core, ADR-004) and checks the porto capsule abi_major at import; douro depends on porto==same minor. Wire CI jobs (rust-test, pytest) for the new crates.
acceptance_criteria: import douro works in CI on Linux/macOS/Windows; importing against a mismatched porto ABI major raises a clear ImportError; cargo-deny passes.

title: oxiform release with OX-1..OX-5 published
description: Gate issue: a tagged oxiform release on PyPI/crates.io containing OX-1..OX-5, which Douro M6 pins (oxiform>=X.Y). Douro M6 tasks that call oxiform depend on this. Record the pinned version and ABI major in douro's pyproject and Cargo.toml.
acceptance_criteria: Release published; douro CI installs it from the index and the OX-1 capsule ABI check passes at import.

title: OX-5: JSON Schema bundle API
description: oxiform must emit a bundle of JSON Schema 2020-12 for many types with shared $defs, a configurable ref_template (e.g. #/components/schemas/{name}), stable collision-free names, and validation vs serialization variants. Douro's OpenAPI generator consumes it.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform tests: bundle of nested/overlapping types yields deterministic names and refs per ref_template, input and output variants differ where expected; schemas validate against the 2020-12 metaschema.

title: OX-3: pair-source decoding in lax mode
description: oxiform must decode a model from key/value pairs (raw query string, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, header and cookie pairs) in lax mode, with wire-name aliases and repeated keys mapped to sequences. Douro synthesizes one params model per handler and source so each source is one decode call.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform tests cover query string, urlencoded, repeated keys -> list[T]/tuple, aliases, Optional missing -> None, lax coercion table; callable through OX-1 from Rust.

title: OX-4: error path prefixes and combined reports
description: oxiform must allow prefixing issue paths with a source (body/query/path/header/cookie) and combining issues from several decode calls into one ValidationError whose to_problem() yields a single RFC 9457 problem. Douro builds its single 422 from this.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform tests: issues from three sources merged into one problem with source-prefixed paths and pointers; stable codes preserved; available via OX-1 structured issues.

title: OX-2: encode against a declared type
description: oxiform must support encode(obj, type=T) that walks the declared type T, not the runtime type, so fields of a subclass outside T are never written. Douro relies on this for return-annotation filtering (security, §33 §6) and response_model.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform test: subclass instance with extra fields encoded as T emits only T's fields; exposed through OX-1.

title: OX-1: oxiform embedding C ABI (PyCapsule)
description: Porto needs oxiform to export a versioned C ABI via PyCapsule (oxiform-abi) usable from another cdylib (douro._native): obtain plan handles (plan_for(type)), decode from a Rust-owned byte buffer with mode (strict/lax), limits and context, encode into a Rust buffer, and return structured issues. Douro links oxiform-abi, never oxiform's engine (single-owner rule, ADR-019). Tracked here; implemented in github.com/m4nd0r4s/oxiform.
acceptance_criteria: Released oxiform version exposes the capsule with an ABI major/minor; a sample PyO3 cdylib in porto/examples decodes and encodes a model through it with no duplicate plan cache.

title: pytest plugin: @pytest.mark.porto, fixtures, reproduce hint
description: `porto.pytest_plugin` registered via `pytest11`: `@pytest.mark.porto` runs async tests under porto.run; `@pytest.mark.porto(deterministic=True, seeds=N)` runs N seeds; fixtures `porto_clock` (advance), `porto_net`, `porto_runtime`. On failure print `Reproduce with PORTO_SEED=<seed>`. Coexists with anyio and pytest-asyncio plugins.
acceptance_criteria: pytester-based tests: marker variants, fixtures, failure output contains the reproduce line, rerun with PORTO_SEED reproduces the failure; no conflict when pytest-asyncio and anyio plugins are installed.

title: S4 gate: deterministic CI job, 1000 seeds x stress scenarios
description: CI job `deterministic`: run chat server, connection pool and pipeline scenarios (plus asyncio-facade and sim-network variants) under explore with 1000 seeds; include seeded-bug fixtures and verify every failing seed reproduces with an identical trace hash across 1000 reruns. Audit and eliminate nondeterminism sources (id()-based ordering, GC/weakref callback timing, dict/set iteration under hash randomization).
acceptance_criteria: S4: 100% of seeded failures reproduce across 1000 reruns (trace hashes identical); job runs nightly and on PRs touching porto-sim/porto-core; a regression that introduces nondeterminism fails the job.

title: porto.testing.run, DeterministicConfig, PORTO_SEED
description: `porto.testing.run(main, *, seed=0, clock="virtual"|"real", autojump=True, network=None, max_steps=10_000_000, **cfg)` and `RuntimeConfig(deterministic=DeterministicConfig(...))`; env `PORTO_SEED` overrides the seed; lane settings ignored with a debug log. Run report includes seed, steps, determinism-breaking flags.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: PORTO_SEED overrides explicit seed; clock="real" uses wall time but seeded scheduling; typed stubs pass pyright strict.

title: porto.testing.net: simulated network, links, partitions, faults
description: `Network` with `add_host(name, ip)`, `link(a, b, latency=(lo, hi), loss, bandwidth)` with latency drawn from the seeded RNG, `partition(groups, at=, heal_at=)`, `fault(host, kind="reset_connections", at=)`, plus `Link`. Sim TCP/UDP sockets implement the same ByteStream/listener APIs as porto.net; sim DNS resolver backed by `Network.hosts`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: echo over sim TCP with latency; partition causes timeouts then heals; reset_connections raises ConnectionResetError on both ends; same seed reproduces identical delivery order; Douro test client sim mode can build on it (API review sign-off).

title: sim I/O driver; refuse real I/O unless allow_real_io
description: Implement the `sim` backend of the porto-io Driver trait. Real sockets are refused (`RuntimeError("real I/O in deterministic mode")`) unless `allow_real_io=True`, which is flagged in the run report as breaking determinism. ABI `io_register` from extensions also routes to sim or fails clearly.
acceptance_criteria: Test: connect_tcp to a non-sim address raises the specified error; allow_real_io run report contains the flag; ABI extension example run under sim fails with a clear message or works over sim sockets.

title: porto-sim: seeded single-lane scheduler policy and step trace
description: Crate `porto-sim` with a scheduler policy that forces exactly 1 lane (Python and Rust tasks share it) and at each decision picks uniformly among all runnable tasks with a seeded `ChaCha8Rng`. Enforce `max_steps`, and record a compact task-switch trace (seed, step, task id/name) with a stable hash for reproducibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: Same seed yields byte-identical trace across 1000 reruns of a 100-task scenario; different seeds yield different interleavings; max_steps exceeded raises a clear error with the trace tail.

title: Virtual clock with autojump for deterministic mode
description: Virtual clock driving `current_time()`, `now_ns` (ABI), Rust `Instant` and the timer wheel. With autojump, when nothing is runnable and only timers are pending, jump to the next deadline instantly. Expose `porto.testing.Clock` with `advance(s)` for manual mode.
acceptance_criteria: A test sleeping 1 hour completes in < 100 ms wall time; manual advance fires timers in order; no wall-clock reads in sim mode (asserted via a clock-read counter).

title: Per-lane runtime metrics and aggregation
description: Per-lane, contention-free counters/gauges aggregated on read: tasks_spawned_total{kind}, tasks_alive{kind}, polls_total, steals_total, steal_attempts_total, park_total, park_seconds_total, injector_depth, local_queue_depth, lifo_hits_total, budget_exhausted_total, io_registrations, io_events_total, timers_active, timers_fired_total, blocking_threads, blocking_queue_depth, slow_steps_total, asyncio_bridged_awaits_total, gil_degraded. `metrics=False` compiles counters to no-ops at runtime. Wire ABI `record_metric` for extension metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Test asserts each counter moves under a targeted scenario; aggregated values equal the sum of lanes; benchmark with metrics on vs off within 1%.

title: Blocking-step watchdog with Python stack capture
description: Lanes publish atomic `step_start_ns`. A watchdog thread (only if `slow_step_threshold` set) wakes every threshold/4; for an overrunning lane it attaches briefly, grabs `sys._current_frames()[lane_thread_id]` (<= 30 frames), logs `porto.slow_step` WARNING once per (task, step) with task name, lane, duration and stack, increments `slow_steps_total`, and logs the final duration at INFO on step end. Disabled or virtual-time-aware in deterministic mode.
acceptance_criteria: Test with `time.sleep(0.3)` in a task logs exactly one WARNING with the sleeping frame and one INFO; no watchdog thread when threshold=None; overhead of step_start publication < 1% on spawn/switch micro-benchmarks.

title: porto.inspect: tasks(), tree(), stats(), dump()
description: Python module `porto.inspect` with frozen dataclasses `TaskInfo`, `ScopeInfo`, `RuntimeStats`, and functions `tasks()`, `tree()`, `stats()`, `dump(file=sys.stderr)` (human-readable scope tree with stacks). Typed stubs in `_core.pyi`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: tree() mirrors nested scopes with shield/deadline flags; dump() output golden test; pyright strict on typing sample.

title: Task registry snapshots via lane inbox at maintenance tick
description: On top of the per-lane intrusive task list (M1 registry), implement the snapshot handshake: requester posts to every lane inbox, each lane copies its list at its next maintenance tick (<= event_interval tasks, immediately if idle). Populate TaskInfo (`state`, `waiting_on` strings like "io:read fd=12", "sleep 1.2s", "lock#7", "join task#33", "scope-exit #9", "asyncio-future", timing fields, steps) and ScopeInfo trees.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: snapshot with lanes=8 under load returns every live task exactly once; busy lane answers within one event_interval; waiting_on string correct for each Pending kind; hot-path spawn/complete benchmark unchanged (< 2% delta).

title: Compat CI: run third-party suites under porto with pass-rate report
description: `tests/compat/` runner that checks out pinned versions of asyncpg, redis-py, httpx, aiohttp, runs their suites under `porto.run(..., asyncio_compat=True)` (via a conftest/loop-factory shim), with Postgres/Redis service containers, and emits per-suite pass-rate plus a diff vs the plain-asyncio baseline. Failing tests are triaged into a tracked expected-failure list with reasons.
acceptance_criteria: CI job `compat` produces a pass-rate table per suite; job fails if any suite drops below its threshold; baseline run under stock asyncio documented so pass rate is computed against tests that pass on asyncio.

title: AnyIO backend injection with ANYIO_TESTED_RANGE and fallback
description: At runtime start with `anyio_backend="native"`: if anyio is importable and within `ANYIO_TESTED_RANGE`, set `sys.modules["anyio._backends._porto"]`, insert into `loaded_backends` when present, and rebind `BACKENDS` to include "porto". Outside the range, fall back to "facade" (AnyIO sees asyncio, runs via auto-hosting) and log at INFO. `"off"` disables both. CI tests the min and max of the range.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for native/facade/off modes; out-of-range version (monkeypatched) falls back with INFO log; anyio.run(..., backend="porto") and plain `anyio` calls inside porto.run both work; CI matrix covers lowest and highest supported AnyIO.

title: AnyIO backend: sockets, DNS, processes, signals, fd waits
description: Implement `connect_tcp`, `connect_unix`, `create_tcp_listener`, `create_unix_listener`, `create_udp_socket` (and connected UDP/Unix datagram variants of the AnyIO version in range), `getaddrinfo`, `getnameinfo`, `wait_readable`/`wait_writable`, `open_process`, `open_signal_receiver` on Porto-native net/process/signals, returning AnyIO stream/listener classes.
acceptance_criteria: AnyIO test_sockets, test_subprocesses, test_signals pass with backend "porto" (documented xfails only); httpx client requests over HTTP/1.1 and TLS work under backend "porto".

title: AnyIO backend: run, cancel scopes, task groups, sync primitives
description: `porto._anyio_backend` implementing `anyio.abc.AsyncBackend`: `run`, `current_token`, `current_time`, `cancelled_exception_class` (porto.Cancelled), `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_if_cancelled`, `cancel_shielded_checkpoint`, `sleep`, `create_cancel_scope` (wraps porto.scope), `current_effective_deadline`, `create_task_group`, `create_event`, `create_lock`, `create_semaphore`, `create_capacity_limiter`.
acceptance_criteria: AnyIO's own test modules for cancel scopes, task groups and synchronization pass with backend "porto" (agreed xfail list documented); level-triggered cancel semantics verified against Trio-style expectations.

title: Auto-hosting: proxy asyncio.Task as current_task in Porto tasks
description: In compat mode, when a Porto task touches an asyncio API that needs `current_task()`, register a lightweight proxy `asyncio.Task` subclass as current task on the facade for the duration of the step via `asyncio._enter_task/_leave_task`; its `cancel()` maps to Porto task cancellation. Handle CPython 3.12-3.14 differences in task bookkeeping (3.14 per-thread task linked list).
acceptance_criteria: Tests on 3.11-3.14 and 3.14t: `asyncio.timeout()` and `asyncio.TaskGroup` work inside a Porto task; proxy.cancel() cancels the Porto task; current_task() is None again after the step; no measurable overhead for Porto tasks that never touch asyncio.

title: Bridge: Porto task awaiting asyncio futures (Pending::AsyncioFuture)
description: In the PyTask driver, on a yielded object with `_asyncio_future_blocking=True`: reset the flag, `add_done_callback(waker_cb)` with a Rust callable, park in `Pending::AsyncioFuture`, resume with None on wake. On Porto cancellation call `fut.cancel()` then deliver `Cancelled`, shielded until the future acknowledges (max 1 s), then abandon with a warning. `asyncio.CancelledError` when the Porto scope is not cancelled is a failure (§15 §5). Count `asyncio_bridged_awaits_total`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: awaiting an asyncio.Future / asyncio.Task / asyncpg-like future from a Porto task returns the result; cancellation propagates to the future; a future that ignores cancel triggers the 1 s abandon warning; foreign CancelledError fails the task; bridged-await overhead micro-benchmark recorded (ST-15: ~1 extra callback).

title: Bridge: Trap as minimal Future duck type in asyncio Tasks (T4)
description: Give `_Trap` a slow-path Future duck type: `_asyncio_future_blocking` returns True, plus `add_done_callback`, `remove_done_callback`, `result`, `cancel`, `get_loop`. The facade resolves the trap through a hidden driver path and completes it via callbacks, so Porto-native APIs (sleep, channels, net) work inside real asyncio Tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: inside an asyncio.Task on the facade, `await porto.sleep`, channel recv, TCP read and lock acquire all work; cancelling the asyncio Task cancels the pending trap without losing data (T3); hot-path Porto task performance unchanged (micro-bench delta < 2%).

title: Facade TLS via sslproto, including start_tls
description: Support `ssl=` on create_connection/create_server/create_unix_* using stdlib `ssl.SSLContext` through asyncio's `sslproto` layered on the Rust transport (correctness over speed). Implement `loop.start_tls()` (needed by asyncpg's SSL upgrade and aiohttp proxies; not named in §22) plus `ssl_handshake_timeout`/`ssl_shutdown_timeout`.
acceptance_criteria: TLS echo with a self-signed CA; start_tls upgrade test; asyncpg connects to Postgres with sslmode=require under porto; aiohttp HTTPS request to a local TLS server passes.

title: Facade TCP/Unix transports: create_connection, create_server
description: Rust transports implementing `asyncio.Transport` with protocol callbacks (`connection_made`, `data_received`, `eof_received`, `connection_lost`), write buffering with high/low water marks driving `pause_writing`/`resume_writing`, `pause_reading/resume_reading`, `BufferedProtocol` (`get_buffer`/`buffer_updated`), `get_extra_info`. Implement `create_connection` (happy eyeballs via Porto DNS), `create_server` returning an `asyncio.Server` (`serve_forever`, `close`, `wait_closed`), `create_unix_connection`, `create_unix_server`, `connect_accepted_socket`. asyncio streams (`open_connection`/`start_server`) work on top.
acceptance_criteria: asyncio streams echo test, flow-control test with a slow reader (pause_writing called), BufferedProtocol test, server close/wait_closed test; ported CPython test_asyncio transport cases pass at the agreed rate.

title: Facade add_reader/add_writer and sock_* operations
description: Implement `add_reader/remove_reader/add_writer/remove_writer` as driver registrations, and `sock_recv`, `sock_recv_into`, `sock_recvfrom`, `sock_sendall`, `sock_sendto`, `sock_connect`, `sock_accept`, `sock_sendfile` with nonblocking ops retried on readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Port the relevant cases of CPython test_asyncio sock_* and reader/writer tests and run them against the facade on epoll, kqueue, IOCP legs; removing a reader inside its own callback is safe.

title: Facade create_future/create_task with real C asyncio.Task
description: `create_future()` returns stdlib `_asyncio.Future(loop=self)`; `create_task(coro, name=, context=)` returns a real C `_asyncio.Task` bound to the facade so asyncio code keeps exact semantics (uncancel, cancel messages, current_task, eager tasks factory where applicable). Support `set_task_factory/get_task_factory`. asyncio Tasks are tracked so they are cancelled when the owning Porto scope exits.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: asyncio.gather/wait/TaskGroup/asyncio.timeout work inside an asyncio Task on the facade; Task.uncancel and cancel(msg) behave like stdlib; asyncio.current_task() inside such a task returns it; tasks left running at scope exit are cancelled.

title: Facade EventLoop pyclass: callbacks, timers, handles, time()
description: Rust pyclass `porto.asyncio.EventLoop(asyncio.AbstractEventLoop)`, one per Python lane, created lazily and registered via `asyncio._set_running_loop` while the lane runs. Implement `call_soon`, `call_soon_threadsafe`, `call_later`, `call_at` with a per-lane callback queue drained like a high-priority task and timers on the wheel; `Handle`/`TimerHandle`-compatible pyclasses (`cancel`, `cancelled`, `when`) with a 256 freelist; `time()` = `porto.current_time()`; exception handler API, `get_debug/set_debug`, `is_running/is_closed`. Callbacks run in their captured contextvars context.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests: `asyncio.get_running_loop()` inside a Porto task returns the lane's facade; call_soon FIFO order; call_later/call_at fire at the right virtual/real time; cancelled handles never run; call_soon_threadsafe from a foreign thread wakes an idle lane; exception handler receives callback errors.

title: porto::compat::hyper: PortoExecutor, PortoTimer, PortoIo
description: Implement `PortoExecutor` (hyper::rt::Executor spawning into the current scope), `PortoTimer` (hyper::rt::Timer on the timer wheel, `Sleep` reset support) and `PortoIo<T>` (hyper::rt::Read/Write over porto AsyncRead/AsyncWrite). Add a hyper client example in `examples/hyper-client` (HTTP/1.1 and h2) and a minimal server smoke test.
acceptance_criteria: examples/hyper-client fetches from a local hyper server over h1 and h2 in CI (M3 exit); server smoke test handles 1k sequential keep-alive requests; timer reset test passes.

title: Rust structured concurrency: porto::scope, drop=cancel, reaper
description: Implement `porto::scope(f) -> impl Future<Output = Result<R, ScopeError>>`, `Scope::{spawn, cancel, deadline, set_deadline}`, and cloneable cancel-only `CancellationToken`. Scope futures own `'static` children; dropping the scope future cancels all children and, if dropped before completion, hands the wait to a runtime-owned reaper so no child outlives without being dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: child error cancels siblings and surfaces as ScopeError; dropping the scope future mid-run cancels children and the reaper observes all child drops before runtime shutdown completes; deadline triggers cancellation; loom model for scope cancel vs spawn race passes.

title: porto crate: runtime::Builder, Runtime, Handle and task module
description: Create the `porto` facade crate re-exporting porto-core/io/net/fs/process/signal. Expose `runtime::Builder` (`lanes`, `io_backend`, `steal`, `enable_python(false)`), `Runtime`, `Handle::{spawn, block_on, current}`, and `task::{spawn (into current scope, panics if none), spawn_blocking, JoinHandle<T>, yield_now, coop::{budget, poll_proceed}, TaskId}`. `block_in_place` deliberately absent. Pure Rust: no pyo3 in the dependency tree.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo tree -p porto` shows no pyo3; tests: Builder with lanes=4 runs 10k spawned tasks; task::spawn outside a scope panics with a clear message; spawn_blocking result returned; passes A1 (`cargo test --workspace --exclude porto-py`).

title: examples/: sample PyO3 extension doing TCP via the ABI
description: Maturin-built example extension (e.g. `examples/porto-ext-echo`) that depends only on porto-pyo3, exposes an async `echo_client(host, port, data)` and an echo server task, and is tested from pytest under `porto.run`. Also build a second independent example cdylib and load both in one process to prove the single-runtime rule (ST-8).
acceptance_criteria: pytest suite in examples/ passes in CI on Linux, macOS, Windows for 3.11-3.14 and 3.14t: TCP echo via ABI, cancellation mid-read leaves no leaked registrations, two extensions share one runtime (same RtHandle identity), wheel built with no porto-core linked (checked via symbol/dependency inspection). This is the M3 exit gate.

title: porto-pyo3 crate: future_into_py, PortoHandle, net::TcpStream
description: Public helper crate for third-party PyO3 extensions: `porto_pyo3::future_into_py(py, fut)` (requires `Send`, converts result on a Python lane), `PortoHandle`, `py_await`, `spawn_py`, and `porto_pyo3::net::TcpStream` re-exporting the porto-abi readiness-based stream. Pin a supported pyo3 version range and document attach/with_gil naming per version.
acceptance_criteria: Doc examples compile (B.5 `fetch_row` sample as a doctest); non-Send future fails to compile (trybuild test); crate passes clippy -D warnings and is publishable (`cargo publish --dry-run`).

title: Safe Rust wrappers in porto-abi (Handle, spawn, scope, sleep, AsyncFd)
description: On top of the raw table, provide RAII types in porto-abi with no pyo3 dependency: `Handle` (current/clone/drop), `spawn`/`JoinHandle`, `Scope` (new, cancel, cancelled future, wait_children), `sleep`/`sleep_until`/`now`, and an `AsyncFd`/`Registration` readiness wrapper, plus `TcpStream`/`TcpListener` built on `io_register`/`io_poll_ready`. Keep these pyo3-free so douro-http (which links porto-abi only, ADR-004) can reuse them.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests against the real capsule (via porto-py test harness) cover each wrapper; dropping wrappers releases handles (leak test); TcpStream echo round-trip passes on Linux/macOS/Windows.

title: Export ABI v1: Python bridge and Trap::AbiFuture
description: Implement `future_into_py` (returns an awaitable yielding `TrapKind::AbiFuture`; result `PyResultPtr` converted on a Python lane), `py_await` (spawns a PyTask in the current scope and exposes its result as FfiFuture), `py_spawn`, `call_soon_py` (run sync callable on a Python lane), and `defer_decref` (safe from any thread, never requires attachment). Enforce the attached-thread requirement for `py_*` functions. Add `task_set_name` and `record_metric` slots (MetricId registration rules to be defined).
acceptance_criteria: Python tests: awaiting a future_into_py awaitable returns value / raises the error object; cancellation of the awaiting task drops the Rust future; py_await of a Python coroutine from Rust returns its result; defer_decref from a non-Python thread frees the object on a lane (refcount test); call_soon_py runs on a Python lane on GIL and 3.14t builds.

title: Export ABI v1 capsule: runtime, task and scope functions
description: In porto-py `abi_export.rs`, create the `_ABI_V1` capsule at module init (valid for process lifetime, I2) and implement `current_runtime`, `runtime_clone/drop`, `spawn`, `spawn_in_scope`, `task_abort/join/drop`, `spawn_blocking`, `scope_current/new/cancel/wait_children/drop`, `cancelled`. Foreign `FfiFuture`s run as Rust tasks in the scope tree with full C4 failure propagation. Every entry point catches unwinds: inside a task poll -> `RustPanic` failure of that task (ADR-027), elsewhere abort after logging. Define behaviour of `spawn` when no current scope exists.
acceptance_criteria: Rust integration tests via a test cdylib: spawn/join returns JoinResult; scope_cancel cancels FFI tasks (drop = cancel); child failure cancels siblings; panicking FFI future surfaces as porto.RustPanic in Python; handle refcounts verified leak-free under a counting allocator; loom/TSAN not required here but tests run with lanes=4.

title: Export ABI v1: time and I/O readiness functions
description: Implement `now_ns`, `sleep_until` (runtime clock, virtualizable later), and `io_register`, `io_poll_ready`, `io_clear_ready`, `io_deregister` on top of porto-io `ScheduledIo` readiness with tick-based clearing. `io_register` returns errno, `io_poll_ready` returns 0=Ready/1=Pending and the ready tick. Works on every driver backend (epoll, kqueue, IOCP-AFD, io_uring multishot poll).
acceptance_criteria: Tests through a test cdylib: register a socketpair, poll pending then ready after write, clear_ready with stale tick does not drop newer readiness, deregister wakes nothing afterwards; sleep_until fires within timer resolution; run on Linux epoll, Linux io_uring, macOS, Windows CI legs.
spec_id: docs/spec/10-porto-runtime/21-rust-api-and-abi.md §B.4; 13-io-driver.md (ScheduledIo, clear_readiness tick, io_uring multishot poll for ABI users)

title: porto_abi::api() capsule discovery and version checks
description: Implement `porto_abi::api() -> &'static PortoApi` cached in a `OnceLock`: import `porto._core`, fetch capsule `_ABI_V1` (named "porto._core._ABI_V1"), check `abi_major == 1` and `struct_size >= size_of::<PortoApiV1>()`. Provide `has_field!`-style helpers so consumers check `struct_size` before touching fields added in later minors. Panic with a clear message when porto is missing or the major mismatches. Must work on 3.11-3.13 where `PyImport_ImportModuleAttrString` does not exist (use import + getattr or `PyCapsule_Import`).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: missing porto -> panic message names the package; fake capsule with abi_major=2 -> mismatch panic; capsule with larger struct_size accepted; field-presence helper returns false for a field beyond a smaller struct_size; runs on CPython 3.11 and 3.14.

title: porto-abi crate: repr(C) PortoApiV1 table and handle types
description: Create crate `porto-abi` with `#[repr(C)] PortoApiV1` exactly as in B.4 (abi_major/abi_minor/struct_size header; runtime, task, scope, time, I/O readiness, Python bridge and observability slots). Define opaque refcounted handles `RtHandle`, `TaskHandle`, `ScopeHandle`, `IoHandle`, plus `SpawnOpts`, `JoinResult`, `PyResultPtr {ok, err}`, `RawFdOrSocket`, `MetricId`, using `async-ffi` `FfiFuture`/`FfiContext`. No Python or porto-core dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Crate builds with no pyo3 dependency; a layout snapshot test asserts size/align/field offsets of PortoApiV1 and every repr(C) type on 64-bit Linux, macOS, Windows; cbindgen-generated `porto_abi.h` is committed and checked for drift in CI.

title: Check and reserve porto/douro names on PyPI and crates.io
description: Before any crate or wheel name is baked into the ABI capsule name (porto._core._ABI_V1), the porto-pyo3 crate, or docs, check availability of PyPI `porto`, `douro`, `porto-console` and crates.io `porto`, `porto-abi`, `porto-pyo3`, `porto-macros`, `porto-sim`, `porto-tokio-bridge`. If taken, pick from the reserve list (ribeira, marea, tejo / cais, vinho) and record the choice as an ADR. Reserve the chosen names with placeholder releases.
acceptance_criteria: ADR added to 04-decision-records.md with the final names; placeholder packages published (or ownership confirmed) on PyPI and crates.io for every name that 51 §4 says will be published; capsule name and crate names in the spec updated if they changed.

title: connect_tcp with Happy Eyeballs v2 (RFC 8305)
description: porto.net.connect_tcp(host, port, *, tls=False, server_hostname=None, local_addr=None, happy_eyeballs_delay=0.25, nodelay=True): resolve via §4, race attempts in an internal scope per RFC 8305 (staggered by happy_eyeballs_delay, cancel losers), check SO_ERROR on Connect readiness. Timeouts come only from the enclosing scope deadline. tls != False raises NotImplementedError until TLS lands.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: unreachable first address falls through to the second after the delay; losing attempts are closed; enclosing move_on_after cancels cleanly with no FD leak; refused maps to ConnectionRefusedError.

title: listen_tcp and TcpListener with EMFILE backoff
description: porto.net.listen_tcp(host=None, port=0, *, backlog=1024, reuse_port=False, tls=None, dual_stack=True) -> TcpListener with await accept(), async for, port, aclose(). Linux uses accept4(SOCK_NONBLOCK|SOCK_CLOEXEC). On EMFILE/ENFILE back off 100 ms with a rate-limited warning, never busy-loop. tls param raises NotImplementedError until TLS lands.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: port=0 reports the bound port; dual_stack accepts v4 and v6; RLIMIT_NOFILE exhaustion test shows backoff (CPU stays idle) and recovery; accepted sockets are CLOEXEC.

title: getaddrinfo resolver with cache and coalescing
description: Default resolver in porto-net dns: getaddrinfo on the blocking pool, per-lane positive cache with 30 s TTL, coalescing of concurrent identical lookups. Python: await porto.net.resolve(host, port=0, *, family=0) -> list[SockAddr]. IP literals bypass the pool.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: 100 concurrent resolves of the same host issue one getaddrinfo (counter); cache entry expires after TTL (injected clock); IP literal resolves without a thread hop; failure maps to socket.gaierror.

title: TcpStream core I/O methods and socket options
description: porto-net TcpStream on ScheduledIo, exposed as porto.net.TcpStream implementing porto.abc.ByteStream: read(max) (b"" at EOF), read_buffer(max) -> Buffer, read_into(buf), write(data) writing all with backpressure, writev(buffers), shutdown_write(), aclose()/async with, set_nodelay, set_keepalive(idle, interval, count), peername, sockname, fileno(). Errno mapping to builtin OSError subclasses (ConnectionResetError, ConnectionRefusedError, BrokenPipeError, TimeoutError).
acceptance_criteria: Tests over loopback: large write completes fully under a slow reader; half-close observed as EOF by peer; reset maps to ConnectionResetError with errno; read_buffer performs no bytes copy (refcount/alloc counter).

title: Trap::Io and IoOp re-execution on readiness
description: Lanes poll the driver when idle (no driver thread). Implement the IoOp enum (Read, ReadInto, Write, Accept, Connect, RecvFrom, SendTo, WaitReadable, WaitWritable) carried by Trap::Io; on WouldBlock the task parks on the registration's interest and the driver re-executes the op on readiness. Dropping a pending Io trap on cancel unregisters wakers and never consumes data (T3).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: fast-path read returns a ReadyAwaitable without scheduler involvement; slow path yields exactly one Trap; test_T3_trap_cancel_safe_read: cancelling a pending read loses no bytes.

title: Registration lifecycle and close-while-waiting
description: Registration::new(source, interest) registers; drop deregisters while keeping the slab slot until the generation bumps. close() deregisters, wakes all waiters with READ_CLOSED|WRITE_CLOSED|ERROR, then closes the FD; waiters raise porto.ClosedResourceError (OSError, errno EBADF).
acceptance_criteria: Test: task waiting on read while another task closes the stream gets ClosedResourceError with errno EBADF; no FD reuse race (closed FD reopened immediately does not wake old waiters).

title: porto-io Driver trait and ScheduledIo readiness slab
description: Create porto-io with the Driver trait (register/reregister/deregister/turn/waker/kind), RawSource, Interest, RegistrationId, DriverKind, DriverWaker. ScheduledIo slab with generation-tagged IDs: readiness AtomicUsize packing READABLE/WRITABLE/READ_CLOSED/WRITE_CLOSED/ERROR/PRIORITY plus a 15-bit tick; waiters (reader, writer, intrusive extra list); clear_readiness(event) that does not clear newer ticks. Python-free (A1).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: readiness packing round-trip, stale-tick clear is a no-op, generation mismatch ignores stale wakers; cargo test -p porto-io without Python.

title: epoll/kqueue backend via mio (edge-triggered)
description: Implement the mio backend for epoll (Linux default) and kqueue (macOS/BSD default) with edge-triggered registration, turn(timeout) dispatching into ScheduledIo, and a cross-thread DriverWaker. Implement io_backend selection for 'auto'|'epoll'|'kqueue'; 'io_uring'/'iocp' fall back with a warning (or error with io_backend_strict) until their backends land.
acceptance_criteria: Tests on Linux and macOS CI: socketpair readiness, waker unblocks turn from another thread, turn honours timeout; io_backend='io_uring' + io_backend_strict=True raises a clear error in M1.

title: Python channel()/unbounded_channel() Sender and Receiver
description: Expose porto.channel[T](capacity) and porto.unbounded_channel[T]() over T = PyObj. Sender: await send, try_send (porto.WouldBlock), clone, close, async with, blocking_send, capacity, is_closed. Receiver: await recv (porto.EndOfChannel when closed and drained), try_recv, async for, clone, close, blocking_recv, await recv_many(max) -> list. Dropping a handle on refcount release equals close; sends to a channel without receivers raise porto.BrokenResourceError.
acceptance_criteria: §16 semantic tests for each method and closure rule; `del rx` makes send raise BrokenResourceError; channel requires a capacity (TypeError without it); recv_many returns up to max items without extra wakeups.

title: Bounded MPMC channel core (Vyukov queue + waiter lists)
description: Implement porto::sync::mpsc generic over T: Send: crossbeam ArrayQueue fast path plus sender/receiver waiter lists under a small mutex, waking exactly one counterpart. Closure: ends when all senders are closed/dropped (receivers drain first) or all receivers dropped (send fails). Unbounded variant behind a separately named constructor.
acceptance_criteria: Rust tests for ordering, capacity, close/drain; loom model 'mpsc close races' passes; no lost wakeups in a 1M-message stress test.

title: Event and Notify primitives
description: porto.Event: set(), is_set(), await wait(); not clearable (Trio semantics). porto.Notify: notify_one() stores a permit when nobody waits, notify_all(), await notified(). Rust sync::Event and sync::Notify are thread-safe and usable from Rust tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: permit stored and consumed once; notify_all wakes all current waiters only; Event.wait after set completes synchronously; loom model for Notify permit races.

title: Intrusive FIFO wait queue with cancel-safe grant handoff
description: Build the shared waiting infrastructure in porto-core sync: intrusive WaitNode (PyTask.wait_node; inside the future for RustTask), FIFO queue, removal on cancellation, and the invariant that a cancelled waiter that was already granted passes the grant to the next waiter. Provide blocking_* waiting for non-runtime threads; calling blocking_* on a lane thread raises RuntimeError.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for FIFO order and cancel removal; loom model 'grant vs cancel' passes; blocking_* from a lane raises RuntimeError, from a plain thread completes.

title: Scope nursery semantics: child failure, exit wait, closed scope
description: Complete Scope.spawn and __aexit__: C3 absorption (cancelled_caught), C4 child failure records the error and cancels the scope, exit raises strict ExceptionGroup("porto scope '<name>' failed", errors) or BaseExceptionGroup with the body exception first; C5 __aexit__ waits via TrapKind::ScopeExit until live_children == 0 and never abandons children; C6 spawn into a cancelled scope starts cancelled; C7 spawn after close raises RuntimeError('scope is closed'); C12 root scope is a nursery and porto.run re-raises main's error after shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests test_C3_*, test_C4_child_failure_cancels_siblings, test_C4_body_exception_first, test_C4_base_exception_group, test_C5_exit_waits_children, test_C6_spawn_into_cancelled, test_C7_spawn_after_close, test_C12_background_failure_cancels_main.

title: Scope deadlines, timeout() and move_on_after() (C3, C9)
description: Arm the scope's deadline TimerEntry (each PyTask embeds one entry for its innermost scope deadline); firing calls scope.cancel_by_deadline(). Effective deadline = min over unshielded ancestors; writing scope.deadline re-arms. On deadline with raise_on_timeout=True the scope raises builtin TimeoutError, else absorbs; expose timed_out. Add porto.timeout(s) and porto.move_on_after(s); scope(timeout=, deadline=) with deadline = inf when unset.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests test_C3_deadline_raises_TimeoutError, test_C3_move_on_after_absorbs, test_C9_deadlines_nest, test_C9_set_deadline_rearms; virtual-clock-free tests use tolerances and assert never-early firing.

title: Level-triggered cancel delivery at checkpoints (C1, C2, C10)
description: Wire Scope.cancel(reason) to bump cancel_epoch and cancel_generation and wake every waiting task in the subtree whose pending trap is cancellable (wakes routed to the owning lane inbox). checkpoint_if_needed raises porto.Cancelled at every checkpoint while effectively cancelled (level-triggered); pure Python between awaits is never interrupted. cancel() is safe from any thread.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests test_C1_level_triggered, test_C2_only_at_checkpoints, test_C10_cancel_from_foreign_thread (cancel from a threading.Thread wakes a task blocked in recv/sleep/lock).

title: Scope tree and effective-cancellation walk
description: Implement ScopeNode/ScopeState in porto-core scope::node: parent link, owner_task, cancel_called: Option<CancelReason> (Explicit|Deadline|Parent|ChildFailed|Shutdown), shield, live_children, child_scopes intrusive list, errors, exit_waiter, cancel_epoch. Implement the effective-cancellation walk (shielded scope's own cancel counts) with the per-task (scope_ptr, epoch) cache and a global cancel_generation so the common check is O(1).
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit tests for the walk over nested/shielded trees covering the 'shielded scope's own cancel counts' rule; criterion bench: cancel check with unchanged generation is a single atomic load; loom model 'scope cancel vs spawn' added to the loom suite.

title: sleep, sleep_until, sleep_forever on the timer wheel
description: Rebase the M0 Trap::Sleep onto the wheel using the TimerEntry embedded in PyTask; Rust Sleep futures embed their own entry. Add porto.sleep(s) (s <= 0 is a pure checkpoint/Yield), porto.sleep_until(deadline) and porto.sleep_forever() -> NoReturn (until cancelled). Cancelling a sleeping task unlinks its entry in O(1).
acceptance_criteria: Python tests: sleep(0) and sleep(-1) behave as checkpoints; sleep_until(current_time()+0.05) never wakes early; sleep_forever only exits via cancellation; cancelled sleeps leave no entry in the wheel (inspect counter).

title: Hierarchical timer wheel (6x64 levels, 1 ms default)
description: Implement time::wheel in porto-core: 6 levels x 64 slots, level-0 slot = resolution, intrusive TimerEntry { deadline_tick, prev, next, waker/state }, O(1) insert and unlink-cancel. deadline_tick rounds up (never fire early); expired entries fire in batches; deadlines beyond ~2.2 years are clamped and re-armed. Python-free (rule A1).
acceptance_criteria: proptest: random insert/cancel/advance sequences match a BTreeMap model (§52 item 1); test that no entry fires before its deadline; clamp/re-arm test for > max span; cargo test passes without Python.

title: Drive the timer wheel from the lane park loop
description: The lane processes its wheel shard during maintenance and before parking. Park timeout = min(next deadline in own shard, driver-provided), with deadline - now rounded up to driver granularity (ms for epoll/kqueue, µs via epoll_pwait2 on Linux >= 5.11). Validate RuntimeConfig.timer_resolution within [100µs, 10ms]. No timer thread exists.
acceptance_criteria: Test: an idle lane with one 50 ms timer parks once and wakes no earlier than the deadline; out-of-range timer_resolution raises at config time; epoll_pwait2 path covered on a Linux >= 5.11 CI runner.

title: Runtime monotonic clock and current_time()
description: Add porto-core time::clock: a Clock abstraction over Instant with the runtime epoch at runtime start, plus a pluggable virtual-clock hook for deterministic mode (§24). Expose porto.current_time() -> float and alias porto.monotonic(). Deadlines are absolute floats in runtime-clock seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit tests: monotonicity, epoch is 0 at start; a test Clock impl can be swapped in (hook used later by porto-sim). Python: current_time() is monotone and monotonic is current_time.

title: GATE: 8 lanes vs N asyncio loops (TCP echo, skewed load)
description: Compare Porto lanes=8 vs 8 threads each running an asyncio loop on 3.14t: TCP echo (uniform) and skewed load (one hot connection pair + many idle). HTTP JSON variant needs Douro and is re-run at M6.
acceptance_criteria: Porto >= 1.3x on TCP echo and >= 2x on skewed load; results published with code.

title: GATE: free-threaded scaling >= 5.6x at 8 lanes
description: Benchmark independent CPU-light Python tasks on 3.14t at 1, 2, 4, 8 lanes on the reference machine.
acceptance_criteria: Throughput at 8 lanes >= 5.6x of 1 lane (0.7 efficiency); results in bench/results.

title: GATE: TSAN clean (porto-core and free-threaded porto-py)
description: Nightly TSAN build of porto-core tests and the Python suite with lanes=8 on a TSAN-built CPython 3.14t. Suppressions file only for documented CPython-internal false positives.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive nightly runs with zero TSAN reports; suppressions reviewed.

title: Free-threaded Python lanes: per-lane thread state and detach
description: On 3.14t each Python lane creates a PyThreadState at start (PyThreadState_New + PyEval_RestoreThread), stays attached while running Python, detaches before parking/blocking so stop-the-world GC proceeds. All Python lanes can step PyTasks; cross-lane deferred decref routing to owner lane.
acceptance_criteria: Test: gc.collect() from a task completes while other lanes are parked; lanes=8 Python suite green on 3.14t; P1 debug asserts never fire.

title: Work stealing: adaptive/off/eager modes
description: steal='adaptive': searching lane picks random victim and steals half via steal_batch_and_pop; 'off' gives thread-per-core semantics (only own spawns and inbox); 'eager' threshold 1. Blocked lane's queued tasks are drained by others (ST-3).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: one lane blocked in sync code -> queued tasks complete on other lanes; steal='off' -> tasks never change lane; mode switch via config.

title: Multi-lane runtime: lane threads, LaneKind, local queue overflow
description: Spawn lanes 1..N-1 as threads; Lane{index, kind: Python|RustOnly, local crossbeam Worker cap 256 with overflow to injector in batches of 128, stealer, park, tick, is_searching, thread_state, metrics, deferred_decref}. Lane kind table per build (GIL N>1: lane 0 Python, others RustOnly; free-threaded N>1: all Python). Lane join on shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Rust runtime with lanes=4 runs 1M tasks spawned from all lanes; overflow test pushes > 256 locally and verifies injector batch move; shutdown joins all lanes.

title: Runtime start, porto.run/Runtime.block_on and invariants I1-I4
description: Runtime NEW->RUNNING: detect build, probe backend, create lane 0 on the caller, install hooks (asyncgen, fork, signal receiver if main thread, import hook on free-threaded), spawn main into root scope. porto.run, Runtime(...).block_on, context manager, runtime(), in_runtime(). I1: second run (or run on a blocking-pool thread) -> RuntimeError. I4: objects hold Arc<RuntimeInner>; use after shutdown -> RuntimeClosed. Signal/AnyIO installation steps are hooks filled by their owners.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: nested run raises; run from to_thread worker raises; run returns main's result / re-raises its exception; Task handle used after shutdown raises RuntimeClosed; sequential runs in one process work.

title: CPython compat layer and build matrix 3.11-3.14t
description: py_compat module: take_exception (PyErr_GetRaisedException >= 3.12, Fetch+Normalize on 3.11), interned strings via PyOnceLock, steal-semantics send wrapper. Module declares Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED. pyclasses frozen; internal mutability via atomics/Mutex. CI grep lint banning borrowed-ref APIs (PyDict_GetItem, PyList_GetItem, PyWeakref_GetObject, ...) in porto-py; critical sections for user-dict iteration.
acceptance_criteria: porto-py builds and the test suite runs on 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.14t; lint job fails on a planted borrowed-ref call; importing porto on 3.14t does not re-enable the GIL.

title: GIL-build attachment policy for lane 0
description: Lane 0 keeps the GIL across consecutive Python tasks, releases before parking and before blocking syscalls; one explicit PyThreadState per lane thread (P0, no PyGILState on lanes). Periodic GIL release every gil_switch_interval (default sys.getswitchinterval()) of continuous Python execution when threading.active_count() > 1 (checked in maintenance).
acceptance_criteria: Test: a background threading.Thread makes progress while lane 0 runs a busy chain of tasks; no GIL release between tasks when no other threads exist (counter).

title: Thread-state rules: PyDeferred and deferred decref queue
description: PyObj owned type whose Drop debug-asserts thread_is_attached(); PyDeferred wrapper whose Drop pushes onto the owning lane's deferred_decref SegQueue, drained at maintenance. Ownership rules for lanes, blocking workers, and non-attached threads. Document and lint P3 (no Rust mutex held across calls into Python).
acceptance_criteria: Debug-build test: dropping PyObj on a non-attached thread panics; PyDeferred dropped on a foreign thread is decref'd on the lane at next maintenance (leak test 0 growth).

title: Lane parking and driver ownership (single lane)
description: Parker (futex-based); when idle the lane blocks in the driver turn with timeout = next timer deadline; unpark from other threads wakes the driver waker (eventfd/kqueue user event). Lane detaches (PyEval_SaveThread) before blocking with nonzero timeout (I3/P2). Integrates the I/O driver and timer wheel delivered by the I/O and time work in M1.
acceptance_criteria: Test: wake from a foreign thread unparks a lane blocked in the driver within 1 ms; a Python thread can run while lane 0 is parked (GIL released).

title: Single-lane scheduler loop, injector and maintenance tick
description: Lane and Shared structs (single lane): local queue, injector for wakes from non-lane threads, tick with event_interval (61) maintenance (non-blocking driver poll, timers, drain deferred_decref) and global_queue_interval (31) injector-first fairness. Lane 0 is the thread calling porto.run. Structured so M2 adds lanes without rewriting the loop.
acceptance_criteria: Fairness test: self-waking task does not starve the injector, which progresses within 2 x global_queue_interval ticks. Rust-only runtime runs 1M trivial tasks.

title: Task spawn core: context copy, naming, pin flag
description: Internal spawn_py / spawn_rust used by Scope.spawn (scope semantics are owned by the scopes work in M1): accepts coroutine or callable+args, PyContext_CopyCurrent by default or context= override, name, pin flag (PIN header flag), scope pointer, registry link, schedule on current lane.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: contextvar isolation parent/child; context= override honoured; pin flag visible via Task.pinned; spawn of non-awaitable raises TypeError.

title: PyTask::poll step algorithm (production)
description: Production step loop: context enter/exit, lane.current_task, budget reset, pending resolution, level-triggered cancel injection via scopes::effective_cancel hook, PyIter_Send/throw, PYGEN_RETURN/ERROR/NEXT handling, Cancelled-belongs-to-cancelling-scope -> TaskOutcome::Cancelled, synchronous continue when pending is immediately ready, YieldThen when budget is 0. AsyncioFuture detection (_asyncio_future_blocking) stored as Pending; bridging is M4.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests cover each PYGEN branch, unsupported-object TypeError, sync-continue (no scheduler round trip, asserted by step counter), budget-exhaustion yield; 3.11-3.14t matrix green.

title: Ready fast path and cooperative budget
description: _Ready awaitable fast path with checkpoint_if_needed (cancel check + budget decrement), budget reset to coop_budget per poll, YieldThen(Ready(v)) at 0 pushed to back of local queue (not LIFO). Rust side porto_core::coop::{budget, poll_proceed(cx)} like Tokio.
acceptance_criteria: Test: a loop of 1000 ready awaits yields every coop_budget awaits and lets a peer task run; Rust test poll_proceed returns Pending at exhaustion.

title: Full TrapKind set and trap rules T1-T4
description: Implement TrapKind Yield, Sleep, Notified(WaitNodeRef), Io{reg,interest,op}, Join, ScopeExit, Future(Pin<Box<dyn Future>>), AbiFuture (type only; ABI is M3). Pending::poll per variant with cancel-safe drop that unregisters wakers (T3). Rule T1/T2 helpers: checkpoint_if_needed() for synchronous completion. Io/Sleep/Notified/ScopeExit resolution plugs into driver/timer/sync/scope modules owned elsewhere in M1.
acceptance_criteria: Python semantic tests test_T1_*, test_T2_checkpoint_on_sync_completion, test_T3_trap_cancel_safe (drop pending trap -> waker unregistered), Rust tests for Future trap.

title: PyTask body, Resume/Pending/TaskOutcome and memory layout
description: PyTaskBody with coro, context, Resume {None, Value, Throw}, Pending (TrapKind mirror + AsyncioFuture + YieldThen), cancel_stack SmallVec<[ScopeRef;2]>, budget, TaskOutcome {Ok, Err, Cancelled}, intrusive JoinWaiters, lazy py_handle, TaskStats; embedded timer entry and wait node (one active wait per task).
acceptance_criteria: Size asserts: body <= 64 B excl. embedded entries and <= 192 B including timer entry and wait node; header+body within ST-11 budget (<= 128 B header incl. list node).

title: Task harness: state transitions and RustTask
description: CAS transitions following Tokio harness.rs: wake (NOTIFIED if RUNNING else SCHEDULED+push), poll start SCHEDULED->RUNNING, poll end Pending (reschedule if NOTIFIED), poll end Ready (COMPLETE, wake joiners, notify scope). RustTask<F: Future> = Header + F + output slot + join waker; JoinHandle<T> internals and drop of the last waker.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for each transition; property test that a task is never polled while RUNNING; Rust-only test suite green without Python (A1).

title: Task Header, vtable and refcounted state word
description: Final #[repr(C)] Header: state AtomicU32 (RUNNING, NOTIFIED, COMPLETE, CANCEL_REQ, JOIN_INTEREST, SCHEDULED, refcount from bit 6), &'static TaskVTable (poll, drop, dealloc, schedule, id hooks), owner_lane, flags (PIN, PYTHON, DETACHED_DROP), monotonic never-reused u64 id, scope pointer, intrusive queue_next, RegistryNode. TaskRef / Waker built on refcount.
acceptance_criteria: static_assert size_of::<Header>() <= 64; unit tests for ref inc/dec, id monotonicity; miri clean.

title: GATE: spike kill criterion - spawn/switch >= 2x asyncio+uvloop
description: Decide go/no-go from spike results. Kill criterion: if spawn and task switch are not >= 2x faster than asyncio+uvloop, stop and redesign (ADR-001 revisited). Pass criterion: §11 absolute micro targets met or within 30% (checkpoint <= 60 ns, Yield switch <= 250 ns, spawn+complete <= 900 ns).
