Outcome recorded as an ADR entry in 04-decision-records.md with numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: GO (M1 starts) or REDESIGN (with written findings and proposal). Results JSON + bench code referenced. M1 epic blocked until GO.

title: Spike: porto.run, scope.spawn, sleep, checkpoint
description: porto.run(main) turns the calling thread into lane 0 and returns main's result or raises its exception. Minimal `async with porto.scope() as s: s.spawn(...)` that waits for children (no cancellation semantics yet), porto.sleep, porto.checkpoint, contextvars copy on spawn and Enter/Exit per step.
acceptance_criteria: Example programs (fan-out 10k tasks, ping-pong via sleep(0)) run; contextvars set in parent visible in child and not leaked back.

title: Spike micro-benchmarks vs asyncio+uvloop (pyperf)
description: pyperf suite under bench/micro/: checkpoint, Yield task switch round trip, spawn+run-to-completion of `async def f(): return 1`, spawn+join 100k trivial tasks, yield ping-pong; identical programs on asyncio+uvloop. Records machine info into bench/results/<date>-<commit>.json. Oneshot channel row is N/A in M0 (no channels).
acceptance_criteria: Suite runs reproducibly on the reference machine (or best available, documented) for CPython 3.14 GIL; results file committed with source.

title: Spike: PyTask step driver with Yield and Sleep traps
description: PyTask body (coro, context, resume, pending) and the step loop: PyIter_Send for send, cached `throw` via PyObject_CallMethodOneArg, Py_TYPE(obj)==TrapType dispatch, bare `yield` as Pending::Yield, unsupported objects -> TypeError thrown into the coroutine. TrapKind::Yield and TrapKind::Sleep{deadline} backed by a simple deadline heap (wheel is M1). py_compat::take_exception for 3.11 vs 3.12+.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: return value, raised exception, yield round trip, sleep ordering, unsupported awaitable -> TypeError, works on 3.11 and 3.14.

title: Spike: _Trap and _Ready pyclasses with am_send and freelists
description: _Trap (frozen, freelist 512) with __await__ returning self, tp_iternext, am_send and throw; trap taken exactly once, reuse raises RuntimeError('trap reused'). _Ready (freelist 1024) whose am_send returns PYGEN_RETURN with no StopIteration allocation. Interned attribute names via PyOnceLock.
acceptance_criteria: Python tests: `await Trap` inside a coroutine chain delivers the sent value; throw re-raises; reuse raises; ready awaitable returns value. Allocation count per ready await is 0 (tracemalloc/refcount probe).

title: Spike crates: minimal porto-core and porto-py (porto._core)
description: Create the minimum to build the spike: porto-core (no Python, Rule A1) and porto-py cdylib exposing porto._core via pyo3/maturin with gil_used=false. Release profile with panic=unwind, LTO. Only what the spike needs; full workspace layout is HK.
acceptance_criteria: `maturin develop` builds porto._core on 3.14 (GIL); `cargo test -p porto-core` passes without Python; `import porto` works.
close_reason: Satisfied by #3 and #4: porto-core has no Python dependency and tests pass; porto-py builds porto._core with gil_used=false; release profile fat LTO + unwind; import works on 3.11/3.14/3.14t

title: Spike: task header, refcounted state and single-lane run queue
description: Minimal Header (state: AtomicU32 with RUNNING/NOTIFIED/COMPLETE/SCHEDULED bits and REF_ONE=1<<6 refcount, vtable, id) and a single-lane loop: local FIFO queue, run(t), park when empty. Wakers clone/drop refs. Enough of the real layout to make the benchmark representative; may be rewritten in M1.
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit tests: wake-while-running reschedules once, wake-after-complete is a no-op, last ref drop frees task (checked under miri or ASAN).

title: M0 — Spike: is the trap protocol fast enough?
description: Minimal porto-py: single lane, PyTask driver and Trap (Yield, Sleep), run, scope.spawn, sleep, checkpoint. No I/O. Validates the riskiest assumption (ST-1) first.
acceptance_criteria: §11 micro targets met or within 30%. If spawn/switch is not >= 2x asyncio+uvloop, stop and redesign (m0-gate-go-no-go).

title: Housekeeping: bootstrap the repo and keep it honest
description: Workspace scaffold, community files mirroring kinemo and hapto, the first CI, docs skeleton and the project section of CLAUDE.md.
acceptance_criteria: A contributor can clone, build, run the checks in CONTRIBUTING and see CI green on main.

title: Spec errata: compat and observability contradictions
description: sniffio must report 'asyncio' in anyio_backend='facade' mode; ADR-014's lazy facade loop vs get_running_loop() on first use (register a cheap shell eagerly); add loop.start_tls() (asyncpg, aiohttp need it); auto-hosting relies on private asyncio._enter_task/_leave_task, reworked in 3.14 (add to 55 risks); watchdog under deterministic mode; from_thread/Portal from a deterministic blocking job must raise; console server binds to localhost by default.
acceptance_criteria: §22-§24 and 55 updated.

title: Spec errata: ABI v1 gaps to fix before freezing the table
description: record_metric takes a MetricId but nothing registers one (add metric_register); spawn with no current scope is undefined and must not panic across extern C; scope_current() ownership (borrowed or +1) unspecified; B.2 uses PyImport_ImportModuleAttrString, which is 3.14-only while the minimum is 3.11; Douro links only porto-abi (ADR-004) but B.5 puts the ABI TcpStream in porto-pyo3: move pyo3-free readiness/TCP wrappers to porto-abi; state that the ABI has no DNS, UDP or TLS.
acceptance_criteria: §21 updated; the v1 table in the spec is the one m3-abi-types implements.

title: Decide which speedup gates which milestone, and task size budgets
description: The spec disagrees: the M0 kill criterion is 2x asyncio+uvloop, §11 says 2.5x, §53 says 3x for spawn+join; §11 calls its table the M1 gate while the roadmap uses it for M0. Size budgets disagree too (header <= 64 B in §11 vs <= 128 B in ST-11; body <= 64 B in §11 vs <= 192 B in §25). Proposed: M0 = kill criterion >= 2x and within 30% of §11; M1 = absolute §11 targets; header <= 64 B, body <= 192 B incl. timer entry and wait node.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR in 04-decision-records.md; §11, §25, §53 and ST-11 agree with it.
close_reason: ADR-034: gates 2x (M0) -> 2.5x + §11 (M1) -> §53 table (1.0); Header <= 64 B, PyTaskBody <= 192 B

title: Decide where the benchmark reference machine runs
description: §53 requires dedicated bare metal (16 physical cores, isolated CPUs or two hosts over 25 GbE). Choose hosting (owned box vs rented bare metal such as Hetzner/Equinix), budget, and who has access. Current default: one rented 16-core bare-metal host with CPU isolation; the M0 kill-criterion measurement runs on a quiet developer machine and is re-run on the reference machine at M1.
acceptance_criteria: Hosting chosen and budgeted; m1-perf-reference-machine unblocked.
close_reason: ADR-033: maintainer's M4 Pro Mac is the reference machine; ratio gates; Linux paths in Docker VM; see 53 §1

title: Decide the docs toolchain (mkdocs-material vs alternatives)
description: The spec says mkdocs-material with API generated from stubs. kinemo instead generates Markdown reference from code (python -m kinemo.docs.markdown) and builds a SvelteKit site, so following the siblings would diverge from the spec. Also re-verify mkdocs-material's maintenance status (its authors announced a successor, Zensical, in 2025). Current default: mkdocs-material + mkdocstrings-python reading .pyi stubs, per spec.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (ADR or note in 50-repository-layout); hk-docs-skeleton follows it.
close_reason: ADR-032: Zensical + mkdocstrings-python from .pyi stubs; mkdocs-material 9.x fallback with the same config

title: Decide Rust edition, pinned toolchain and MSRV policy
description: The spec only says 'pinned stable'. kinemo and hapto use edition 2021 with no rust-toolchain.toml. Proposed default: edition 2024, rust-toolchain.toml pinned to the current stable and bumped deliberately, and for the published crates (porto, porto-abi, porto-pyo3) an MSRV of N-2 stable releases checked in CI from M3.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded as a new ADR; hk-cargo-workspace and m3-ci-rust-api follow it.
close_reason: ADR-031: edition 2024, rust-toolchain pinned to latest stable (1.99.1), published crates MSRV = pin minus 2 minors

title: Gate: every spec MUST maps to a test
description: Switch the traceability script from informational to gating: CI fails when a MUST rule ID in the spec has no test. Close the gaps it reports or record explicit, reviewed exemptions (e.g. MUSTs verified by benchmarks or conformance suites, linked to those jobs).
acceptance_criteria: Traceability matrix shows zero uncovered MUSTs; CI fails when a new MUST is added without a test.

title: Stability, versioning and support policy docs
description: Docs page stating SemVer guarantees for the Python packages and Rust crates after 1.0, the deprecation period, the porto/douro minor lockstep, the ABI policy (abi_major bumps; all supported majors exported for at least 2 minors), the Python support policy (3.11+, 3.14t+, new CPython within N weeks of release), MSRV policy and security support window. SECURITY.md supported-versions updated to match.
acceptance_criteria: Page published in the docs; SECURITY.md and README link to it; policy referenced by the release checklist.

title: Security review: threat model, internal audit, external review
description: Write docs/security/threat-model.md (HTTP engine, TLS, limits, multipart, static files, console server, ABI boundary). Internal pass: verify every §40 default and rule by test, audit all unsafe blocks for SAFETY justification, run Miri on porto-core data structures where supported. Commission an external review of the HTTP engine and ABI before 1.0; fix or document every finding.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model merged; §40 checklist with linked tests; unsafe audit report; external review report received with zero open high/critical findings.

title: Release publishing for all packages and crates with provenance
description: Extend the release workflow: PyPI Trusted Publishing for porto, douro and porto-console with PEP 740 attestations; crates.io publishing for porto, porto-abi and porto-pyo3 (trusted publishing, ordered by dependency); GitHub release with changelog section, wheels and console binaries plus build provenance attestations. Preflight additionally checks lockstep versions across porto/douro and cargo-semver-checks.
acceptance_criteria: A release candidate tag publishes all artifacts to TestPyPI and a crates.io dry run with attestations visible; a version mismatch fails preflight.

title: Full wheel matrix for porto, douro and porto-console
description: Extend release.yml to CPython 3.11-3.14 and 3.14t (plus later t builds) x manylinux_2_28 (x86_64, aarch64), musllinux_1_2 (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (arm64, x86_64), Windows (x86_64, arm64) for porto and douro, and the console binary per platform. Every wheel is installed on a clean runner (or emulated container) and runs a smoke program; auditwheel/delocate checks pass; sdists build from source.
acceptance_criteria: workflow_dispatch builds and smoke-tests the whole matrix green; wheel tags match the matrix exactly; no wheel exceeds an agreed size budget.

title: 72-hour soak job at 80% capacity
description: Soak harness: a Douro app exercising HTTP JSON, h2, WS, SSE, DB mock, background tasks and the asyncio facade, driven by oha at 80% of the measured max RPS for 72 h. It samples RSS, FD count, task registry size and p99 every minute and fails if RSS grows more than 5% after warmup or FDs grow at all. Weekly schedule on the reference (or a second dedicated) machine; results plotted into the job summary.
acceptance_criteria: One full 72 h run passes with the RSS and FD series attached; a planted per-request leak fails a shortened (2 h) run of the same harness.

title: Fuzzing campaigns before 1.0
description: Run long campaigns on every fuzz target (router, request head, multipart, WS codec; JSON via oxiform): at least 24 CPU-hours per target with ASAN, coverage-guided corpus growth tracked with cargo fuzz coverage. Set up ClusterFuzzLite (or OSS-Fuzz application) for continuous fuzzing after 1.0. Triage, fix and add regression tests for every finding.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign log with hours and coverage per target; zero open crashers; every fixed crasher has a regression test; continuous fuzzing configured.

title: API reference from stubs, runnable examples and coverage check
description: Generate the API pages for porto and douro from python/**/*.pyi and docstrings (mkdocstrings-python or the chosen generator). Every fenced Python example in docs and docstrings runs under pytest (markdown doctest collector) in CI. scripts/doc_coverage.py lists public names (__all__ of porto and douro modules) without a reference entry or without a runnable example and fails when any are missing (S7).
acceptance_criteria: Docs CI fails when a public symbol lacks docs or an example, or an example raises; coverage report shows 100% for the M7 surface.

title: Douro end-to-end CI job with SIGTERM zero-loss check
description: Job running the Douro e2e suite over real sockets: TLS, h2 via httpx and h2load, and the graceful-shutdown test that sends SIGTERM to the supervisor mid-load and asserts every request either completed or was properly refused (zero lost). Linux and macOS; Windows uses Ctrl-Break.
acceptance_criteria: e2e job green on Linux and macOS; the shutdown test reports counts (sent, completed, refused, lost=0) in the job summary.

title: HTTP benchmark suite and competitor apps in the perf job
description: bench/http/: oha/wrk2 scenario definitions (plaintext, JSON, path param + 5-field model, POST 1 KiB validated, 20-query mock DB, SSE fan-out 10k, WS echo; h1 keep-alive 256 conns plus h2 variant) and bench/http/apps/ with pinned competitor apps (FastAPI+Uvicorn, FastAPI+Granian, Litestar+Granian, Granian RSGI, Robyn, BlackSheep, Emmett, Go net/http, Axum) and a porto raw-handler baseline. The nightly perf job runs the M6 scenarios and enforces the §53 §4 gates (5x Uvicorn, 3x Granian, >= 1.0x raw RSGI, framework tax <= 20%, p99 at 70% load <= 2x p50).
acceptance_criteria: Nightly summary shows every gate with numbers; each competitor app starts from its pinned lockfile on the reference machine; results files include competitor versions.

title: ABI compatibility job with the examples/ extension
description: CI job that builds the sample PyO3 extension in examples/ (as its own wheel, against porto-abi from crates path) and tests it against the porto wheel, including a build of the extension pinned to the previous released porto-abi minor to prove additive compatibility (struct_size check). Add examples/ to the layout (§50 does not list it).
acceptance_criteria: Job green; removing a field from PortoApiV1 or reordering it fails the old-minor leg; extension imports and does TCP via the ABI in the test.

title: Publishable crates metadata, semver checks and docs.rs build
description: Give porto, porto-abi and porto-pyo3 full crates.io metadata (description, readme, keywords, rust-version per dec-msrv-edition, docs.rs features) and keep every other crate publish = false. CI: cargo publish --dry-run for the three, cargo doc with -D warnings (RUSTDOCFLAGS) and missing_docs denied for them, an MSRV build, and cargo-semver-checks against the last release once one exists.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run publish succeeds for the three crates and refuses the internals; a missing doc comment on a public item fails CI; the MSRV leg builds.
spec_id: docs/spec/50-engineering/51-build-ci-release.md §4 (porto, porto-abi, porto-pyo3 published; internals publish = false)

title: Nightly porto-py tests under TSAN-built CPython 3.14t
description: Build CPython 3.14t with --with-thread-sanitizer (cached by version), build porto-py with -Zsanitizer=thread, and run the Python suite with lanes=8 nightly. Uses CPython's own TSAN suppressions only; porto-specific suppressions need a comment. This is the M2 exit gate 'TSAN clean'.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly run green on the M2 suite; an injected cross-lane race in a test extension is reported; cache keeps the job under 60 minutes.

title: Free-threaded scaling suite in the perf job
description: Add 3.14t runs to the nightly perf job: independent CPU-light tasks at 1 and 8 lanes (gate >= 5.6x), and Porto 8 lanes vs 'N asyncio loops on N threads' on TCP echo (>= 1.3x) and the skewed load (>= 2x, ST-2). Gates reported as pass/fail in the summary and enforced from M2 exit.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly summary shows the three §53 §3 gates; a run with stealing disabled fails the skewed-load gate.

title: Free-threaded 3.14t legs in py-test
description: Add 3.14t to the py-test matrix on Linux, macOS and Windows, running the suite with lanes=1 and lanes=8. The job asserts sys._is_gil_enabled() is False after importing porto (module declared gil_used = false), so an accidental GIL re-enable fails CI.
acceptance_criteria: 3.14t legs green on main; importing a module that re-enables the GIL in the test env fails the assertion step.

title: Nightly perf job with 5% regression gate and committed results
description: Nightly workflow on the reference runner: run bench/micro (criterion + pyperf, incl. TCP echo 1 KiB x 100 conns and 1M sleeping tasks), compare against the previous result and the §53 gate ratios, fail on any regression over 5%, and commit bench/results/<date>-<commit>.json with machine info via a bot commit. scripts/bench_compare.py renders a Markdown table for the job summary. Later milestones append their suites (m2-ci-perf-scaling, m6-ci-perf-http).
acceptance_criteria: Nightly run commits a results file; an artificial 10% slowdown fails the job; the summary shows each §53 §2 gate as pass/fail.
notes: ADR-033: no hosted perf runner for now; the 'job' is bench/run_reference.sh run nightly on the Mac via launchd.

title: Set up the reference-machine benchmark run on the Mac
description: Per ADR-033 / 53 §1: bench/run_reference.sh runs the pyperf/criterion suites on the maintainer's M4 Pro with the run rules (AC power, warm-up, uv PGO+LTO Python, >= 20 values, <= 8 lanes on P-cores), writes results with a machine fingerprint to bench/results/, and compares with the last committed result (> 5% regression fails). A launchd agent runs it nightly. Linux epoll/io_uring legs run in the Docker Desktop VM, ratios only.
acceptance_criteria: One nightly run produces a committed result with fingerprint; a forced 10% slowdown is reported as a regression.

title: Audit job: cargo deny, cargo audit, pip-audit
description: deny.toml: license allowlist consistent with dual MIT/Apache-2.0 distribution (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, OpenSSL-style notices for aws-lc only), bans (no openssl-sys per ADR-026, no duplicate major versions of tokio/hyper without exceptions), sources (crates.io only, git deps listed). CI job runs cargo deny check, cargo audit and pip-audit on PRs touching lockfiles and on a daily schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Job green on main; adding openssl-sys or a GPL crate fails cargo deny; an advisory in the lockfile fails cargo audit.

title: Loom CI job: PR subset and nightly exhaustive run
description: Job running RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p porto-core --features loom --release. PRs touching porto-core run with LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS=2; a scheduled nightly run uses the full bound with a long timeout and LOOM_CHECKPOINT_FILE to resume. Failures upload the loom trace. The models themselves (task state machine, Notify, Semaphore grant-vs-cancel, mpsc close, scope cancel vs spawn) are M1 runtime issues.
acceptance_criteria: Both workflows green with the M1 loom suite; a seeded bug in a model fails the PR job; nightly results visible in Actions.

title: Full py-test matrix: 3.11-3.14 on Linux, macOS, Windows
description: Grow py-test to the spec matrix (3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14) on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-14, windows-latest. Build the wheel once per OS and Python version (no abi3, so one wheel per version) and install it into test jobs, as kinemo does. Pull requests run oldest and newest Python; main runs all. Free-threaded and io_uring legs are added by m2-ci-free-threaded and m8-ci-io-uring.
acceptance_criteria: Main runs the 4x4 matrix green; PRs run the reduced matrix; tests run against the installed wheel, not the source tree.

title: CI benchmark job for micro benchmarks on main
description: Like kinemo's benchmarks job: on pushes to main run the bench/micro pyperf suite (spawn+join, task switch) against asyncio and asyncio+uvloop on CPython 3.14, write bench/results-format JSON with machine info, show a ratio table in the job summary and keep a benchmarks-<sha> artifact. Shared runners are noisy, so this job is informational; the gating perf job comes with the reference machine (m1-ci-perf-nightly).
acceptance_criteria: A main push produces the summary table and artifact; the JSON includes CPU model, kernel, Python build flags, commit and per-bench ratios vs uvloop.

title: CI lint banning borrowed-reference C APIs in porto-py
description: Add a lint step (scripts/check_borrowed_refs.py) that greps crates/porto-py and crates/douro-py for borrowed-reference APIs (PyDict_GetItem, PyDict_GetItemString, PyList_GetItem, PyWeakref_GetObject, PyTuple_GetItem outside allowlisted spots, pyo3 *_borrowed helpers) and requires the *Ref variants. An allowlist comment marks justified exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Lint job fails on a file using PyDict_GetItem and passes with PyDict_GetItemRef or an allowlist comment with a reason.

title: CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY policy
description: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md: Contributor Covenant 2.1 summary exactly as kinemo. SECURITY.md in kinemo's format: private reporting via GitHub Security tab, response within a week, fix or plan within thirty days. Scope tailored to porto/douro: in scope are HTTP parsing and request smuggling, limit bypasses (§40 defaults), path traversal in File/StaticFiles, TLS misconfiguration, memory safety in porto-core/porto-py/the ABI, the console server listening beyond its configured address; out of scope is running untrusted Python code. Supported versions: latest 0.x until 1.0, then latest minor.
acceptance_criteria: Both files present; GitHub shows the security policy; issue template config links to it.
close_reason: CoC and SECURITY merged in #2; private vulnerability reporting needs the repo public (404 while private)

title: CONTRIBUTING with porto's check commands and conventions
description: Mirror kinemo's structure: Set up (pinned Rust via rust-toolchain.toml, Python 3.11+, uv, maturin develop -m packaging/porto/pyproject.toml), Check your change (cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo nextest run --workspace; uv run ruff check/format --check; uv run pyright; uv run pytest -q), Measure performance (bench/micro, bench/results), and Conventions: English everywhere, descriptive names, small modules, every error has a stable code and says what to do (§26), public API typed under pyright strict, unsafe blocks carry SAFETY comments, no borrowed-reference C APIs in porto-py, test names carry spec rule IDs (test_C4_child_failure_cancels_siblings), a towncrier fragment per user-visible change, small imperative commits. Add a 'What belongs where' section (porto-core vs porto-py vs douro; native code reaches the runtime only via porto-abi, ADR-004) and Licensing (dual license, regenerate THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md).
acceptance_criteria: Every command listed runs green on the scaffold; the same command list appears in the PR template and CI.

title: README in the kinemo/hapto voice
description: README.md: one-line pitch for Porto (Tokio of Python: trap protocol, structured concurrency, lanes, Rust I/O) and Douro (one crossing per request), honest State section (pre-alpha, spec-driven, current milestone), the 30-second tour from the spec README marked as target API, links to docs/spec and the roadmap, supported Pythons (3.11-3.14, 3.14t), and the License section. Keep it short and plain like hapto's README; no benchmark claims until bench/results exist (53 §5).
acceptance_criteria: README renders on GitHub, every relative link resolves (checked by the docs link test once hk-docs-skeleton lands), and it states the license and status.

title: Third-party license script for the shipped Rust crates
description: Port kinemo's scripts/third_party_licenses.py: read cargo metadata, list each crate compiled into a wheel with its SPDX license and copyright lines, and reproduce each distinct license text once. Porto ships several wheels (porto from porto-py, later douro from douro-py and porto-console), so the script takes the root crate and writes one THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md section per wheel (or one file per packaging dir). Include the platform-specific crates (windows-sys, aws-lc-rs and its bundled AWS-LC notices).
acceptance_criteria: Running the script is idempotent; CI fails when Cargo.lock changes without regenerating the file (git diff --exit-code); the porto wheel contains its THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md.

title: Lint and type-check configuration (ruff, pyright strict, pytest)
description: Configure ruff (lint + format, target py311) in the root pyproject, pyright strict over python/ and tests/typing/ (the spec's lint job uses pyright --strict, unlike kinemo's standard mode), and pytest (testpaths tests/python, markers for slow/compat/deterministic). Add tests/typing/ with a first strict sample and .editorconfig. One command list here is what CONTRIBUTING, the PR template and CI all run.
acceptance_criteria: uv run ruff check, uv run ruff format --check, uv run pyright and uv run pytest -q all pass on the scaffold; a deliberately untyped sample in tests/typing fails pyright.
close_reason: Lint/type/test config merged in #6; canonical check list in CLAUDE.md passes on main

title: Public API typing: py.typed, _native.pyi, pyright strict
description: Ship py.typed and complete _native.pyi; all names in §43 fully typed; pyright strict samples under tests/typing exercising decorators, Depends, Annotated markers and responses.
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict on tests/typing passes in CI; public names list matches §43 (test).

title: Mount ASGI apps (HTTP, WebSocket, lifespan)
description: app.mount(prefix, asgi_app) converts requests to ASGI 3.0 HTTP/WebSocket scopes with root_path; receive/send as Rust awaitables; app runs as a real asyncio Task on the lane's facade loop; mounted apps get lifespan events during Douro's lifespan.
acceptance_criteria: Starlette and FastAPI sample apps pass their HTTP and WS tests when mounted; benchmark comparable to FastAPI on Granian ASGI.

title: --reload file watcher
description: notify-based watcher on the app package plus --reload-dir, debounced 100 ms, restarting workers via the supervisor; rejected with --preload.
acceptance_criteria: Test: editing a file restarts workers once per burst; --reload --preload errors.

title: ServerConfig via oxiform.config and precedence
description: douro.ServerConfig as @ox.config (env_prefix DOURO_, env_nested __) with sources pyproject [tool.douro], douro.toml, .env, env, CLI mapping; precedence CLI > env > file > App(server=) > defaults; TLS key material as ox.Secret; douro config explain via cfg.origin.
acceptance_criteria: Precedence matrix tests; config explain shows origins; secrets never printed.

title: Streaming multipart parser, Form/File/UploadFile
description: multer-like streaming multipart/form-data parser on the body stream with per-part limits (max_multipart_parts 100, max_file_size 10 MiB, max_form_fields, max_form_field_size); UploadFile with raw filename and safe_filename sanitized for traversal; Form()/File() params; request.form(); test client files=. Fuzz target.
acceptance_criteria: Limit tests per field, safe_filename traversal cases, large uploads streamed with bounded memory, fuzz smoke passes.

title: File responses: sendfile, Range, ETag, conditional
description: douro.FileResponse(path, filename, media_type, content_disposition, etag, last_modified, root=): sendfile on Linux plaintext else 256 KiB read-ahead; Range (single and multi), If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since -> 206/304/416 in Rust; root= confinement rejects symlinks escaping the root.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for 200/206/304/416, sendfile path used on Linux plaintext, symlink escape rejected.

title: Server-Sent Events: EventStream and Event
description: EventStream(source, ping=15.0, retry) with Event(data, event, id, retry) and dict -> JSON data; Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache, comment pings while idle, Last-Event-ID available via request.headers.
acceptance_criteria: Wire-format tests per field, ping timing under virtual time, reconnect with Last-Event-ID.

title: before_request, after_response and on_error hooks
description: Per-app/per-router hooks compiled into the plan: before_request may return a Response to short-circuit; after_response runs post-send and cannot modify the response; on_error observes failures.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for short-circuit, post-send timing, immutability of sent response, router-level scoping.

title: Stream response with backpressure and disconnect
description: douro.Stream(iterable, media_type) over async or sync iterables (sync iterated on the blocking pool); producer runs in the request scope; each chunk awaited until written with at most 64 KiB in flight per stream; disconnect applies on_disconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: slow client bounds memory to 64 KiB in flight; disconnect cancels producer; sync iterable never blocks the Python lane.

title: Metrics (Prometheus) and HealthCheck layers
description: Metrics(path=/metrics) served in Rust with per-route latency histograms and counters; HealthCheck(path=/healthz, ready_path=/readyz) with readiness flipping to not-ready during shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Scrape test parses exposition format; /readyz returns 503 after shutdown begins while in-flight requests complete.

title: Rust access log and Python logging integration
description: AccessLog(format=json|combined, sample) written by a dedicated Rust logging task with a bounded queue to stderr or file; drops counted in douro_access_log_dropped_total. douro and porto Python loggers with structured JSON handler in production and pretty output in dev.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: log line formats, sampling, drop counter increments when the queue is full, no Python crossing per request.

title: Compression layer: zstd, br, gzip streaming encoders
description: Compression(algorithms=("zstd","br","gzip"), min_size=1024, level) negotiated by Accept-Encoding (q-values), only for compressible types and sizes >= 1 KiB, streaming encoders on the connection's Rust lane, works with streaming responses; Vary: Accept-Encoding set. Off by default.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiation tests, round-trip decode per algorithm, small/incompressible bodies untouched, streaming responses compressed incrementally.

title: Layers: RequestId, Timeout, TrustedHosts, ProxyHeaders, SecHeaders
description: RequestId(header, generate=uuid7, trust_incoming) sets request.id, response header and log field; Timeout(seconds) default route timeout; TrustedHosts patterns -> 400; ProxyHeaders(trusted CIDRs, forwarded) fixes scheme/client IP; request.url uses Host only when validated/trusted; SecurityHeaders (hsts, csp, frame_options DENY, ...).
acceptance_criteria: Tests per layer incl. untrusted proxy headers ignored and Host not trusted without TrustedHosts/ProxyHeaders.

title: CORS layer with Rust preflight
description: Cors(allow_origins list or regex, allow_methods, allow_headers, expose_headers, allow_credentials, max_age); preflight answered entirely in Rust; credentials + wildcard combination handled per Fetch spec.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight and simple-request test matrix; preflight never enters Python.

title: HTTP benchmark harness and competitor apps
description: bench/http with oha/wrk2 drivers (256 conns, h1 keep-alive and h2 variants), scenarios plaintext, JSON, path-param + 5-field model, POST 1 KiB validated; competitor apps (FastAPI+Uvicorn, FastAPI+Granian, Litestar+Granian, Granian RSGI, Robyn, BlackSheep, Emmett, Go net/http, Axum) with exact pinned versions; a porto raw HTTP handler baseline for framework tax; results to bench/results/<date>-<commit>.json with machine info.
acceptance_criteria: Harness reproduces all scenarios on the reference machine with one command; results JSON committed with machine info.

title: Douro end-to-end suite: sockets, TLS, h2
description: Real-socket e2e tests with httpx and h2load over h1, h2, h2c and TLS covering routing, params, bodies, errors and limits; fuzz targets for request head (via hyper). Runs in CI on Linux and macOS.
acceptance_criteria: CI job green; fuzz smoke targets run without findings.

title: Lifespan, app scope, app.state and Background
description: Run lifespan in the app scope (child of worker root); background scope as child of the app scope; douro.Background.spawn owned by it (errors logged and counted, never crash, cancelled after graceful_timeout at shutdown); app.state, request.state, State("key") injection.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: lifespan setup/teardown order, background task survives request, background error counted not raised, cancellation at shutdown.

title: Response classes, Headers multimap and response sink
description: douro.responses: Response, JSON(serializer=), Text, HTML, Redirect(307), NoContent, Problem (RFC 9457); douro.Headers case-insensitive multimap; injectable Response sink with headers and set_cookie(..., secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="lax") merged into the final response.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests per class; cookie defaults Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; sink headers merge with handler-returned response.

title: Lane placement: GIL lanes=2, free-threaded lanes=auto
description: Connections are Rust tasks in the server scope, requests child scopes, handlers PyTasks spawned via py_spawn. GIL build: default lanes=2 (HTTP/TLS on Rust lane, handlers on lane 0). Free-threaded: lanes="auto" (physical cores, max 16) with soft affinity of connection and handler; startup prints the mode.
acceptance_criteria: Tests on GIL and 3.14t builds assert handler lane placement and printed mode; TSAN run of Douro e2e on 3.14t clean.

title: douro.Limits defaults and load shedding
description: Implement douro.Limits with all defaults (max_header_bytes 16 KiB, max_headers 100, max_uri_bytes 8 KiB, max_body_size 1 MiB, max_json_depth 64, form limits, timeouts, max_concurrent_requests_per_lane, h2 limits, ws_max_message_size) and wire them to engine and oxiform ox.Limits. max_queue_wait 5 s load shedding -> 503. Error bodies never contain tracebacks unless debug.
acceptance_criteria: One test per limit asserting the documented status/behaviour at the default and with an override; 503 shedding test under synthetic overload.

title: Route timeouts, disconnect detection, on_disconnect
description: Request scope deadline = route.timeout -> 504 problem if headers not sent, else h2 RST_STREAM / h1 close. Detect disconnects (h1 read-side EOF/RST with read interest during handler, h2 RST_STREAM/close) and apply on_disconnect: cancel (default), ignore (response discarded), CancelAfter(seconds).
acceptance_criteria: e2e tests: timeout 504 before headers and abort after headers; client abort cancels handler (cancel), handler completes (ignore), grace period honored (CancelAfter).

title: HTTP/2 and h2c prior-knowledge with reset mitigation
description: h2 settings: max_concurrent_streams 100, initial windows 1 MiB stream / 2 MiB conn, max_header_list_size 16 KiB, keep-alive ping 20 s/20 s, hyper rapid-reset mitigations plus per-connection reset limit 100/10 s -> GOAWAY. h2c only by prior knowledge (no Upgrade: h2c).
acceptance_criteria: h2load runs clean; rapid-reset attack script triggers GOAWAY; Upgrade: h2c is ignored and served as h1.

title: TLS via rustls with ALPN h2/http1.1
description: TlsStream<PortoAbiStream> driving rustls::ServerConnection inside the adapter; ALPN selection feeding hyper-util's auto builder; ConnState.tls_info/alpn populated; handshakes of Rust-only streams run on Rust lanes when lanes > 1.
acceptance_criteria: e2e tests: httpx over TLS for h1 and h2, invalid cert config errors at startup, ALPN negotiation matrix.

title: Route conflicts, 405/Allow, auto OPTIONS/HEAD, url_for
description: At freeze detect duplicate shapes, param vs catch-all clashes and inline-type vs annotation mismatches, with errors naming both handlers and source locations. Precompute Allow per path shape for 405; auto-answer OPTIONS (204 + Allow) and derive HEAD from GET (body discarded, length kept). Implement app.url_for(name, **params) with names defaulting to __qualname__.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for each conflict error message, 405 Allow contents, OPTIONS/HEAD behaviour, url_for round-trip incl. catch-all and escaping.

title: Path normalization and slash redirects
description: Before matching: reject non-/ raw paths (except * for OPTIONS) with 400, per-segment percent-decode, reject %2F unless allow_encoded_slash, resolve ./.. (above root -> 400), merge_slashes redirect|reject|allow, invalid UTF-8 -> 400, redirect_slashes 308 to canonical form. Add a cargo-fuzz target for normalization.
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven tests per rule; fuzz target runs in CI smoke for 60 s without panics.

title: Confirm oxiform.config features needed by douro.ServerConfig
description: Verify oxiform ships @ox.config with env_prefix, env_nested, sources pyproject/file/dotenv/env/mapping, cfg.origin and ox.Secret, as used by douro.ServerConfig. The spec's OX table does not list these; file oxiform requests for anything missing.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist confirmed against an oxiform release, or follow-up oxiform issues filed and linked.

title: OX-6: encode_into Rust-owned buffer with size hint
description: oxiform should encode directly into a Rust-owned growable buffer (Vec<u8>/BytesMut supplied through OX-1) and expose a size hint, so response bytes never become a Python bytes object (R4, R5 lane-local buffer pools).
acceptance_criteria: Encode via OX-1 into a caller buffer with zero intermediate allocation (verified by allocation counter test); size hint within 2x of actual on benchmark models.

title: porto.testing.explore and hypothesis seeds() strategy
description: `explore(main, seeds=range(1000), stop_on_first_failure=True)` runs many seeds and reports failing seeds with a minimal step trace (task-switch log, trimmed to the tail before failure). `porto.testing.strategies.seeds()` integrates with hypothesis (shrinks toward small seeds).

title: Deterministic mode for the asyncio facade
description: Schedule facade callbacks (call_soon, done callbacks, timer handles) through the same seeded chooser and virtual clock, so asyncio-native code inside deterministic runs is reproducible.

title: Deterministic blocking pool, PYTHONHASHSEED warning
description: In deterministic mode, blocking-pool jobs (to_thread, FS fallback) run synchronously on the lane at the scheduling point without advancing virtual time. Define behaviour of `from_thread.run` from such jobs (error rather than deadlock). Warn when PYTHONHASHSEED is not set.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: to_thread result ordering identical across reruns; from_thread.run inside a sim job raises a clear error; warning emitted exactly once when PYTHONHASHSEED unset.

title: Ship porto-console wheel + binary; console demo
description: Package `porto-console` as a separate wheel (packaging/porto-console/pyproject.toml) and standalone binary; add `examples/console-demo` (chat server with a deliberate slow step) and a recorded demo (asciinema) showing task tree, lanes and slow-step log.
acceptance_criteria: Wheel installs and launches `porto-console` on Linux/macOS/Windows; demo script runs end-to-end in CI (headless smoke) and the recording is linked from docs. M5 console exit gate.

title: porto-console ratatui TUI
description: `porto-console host:port` binary crate with views: task list (sortable by busy time and state), scope tree, lanes (queue depth, park %, steals/s), slow-step log. Reconnects on server restart.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot tests of each view with ratatui TestBackend against recorded JSON fixtures; manual demo script documented.

title: Console server: lane-0 Rust task serving JSON snapshots
description: With `console="host:port"`, run a Rust-only task on lane 0 serving length-prefixed JSON snapshots (`tasks`, `tree`, `stats`, `slow_steps`) and accepting `dump` and `cancel <task_id>` (debug mode only). Versioned wire schema documented; default bind localhost.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: client connects, receives each snapshot kind matching the schema; cancel rejected outside debug mode and works inside; server holds no Python reference and never attaches.

title: Debug mode extras: spawn sites, origin tracking, warnings, P1 asserts
description: With `debug=True` (or PORTO_DEBUG=1, -X dev): spawn-site capture (TaskInfo.spawned_at), coroutine origin tracking, never-awaited trap warnings, swallowed-cancellation warnings (C11), threading.local migration warnings (ST-5), P1 assertions (Py objects on wrong threads), and slow-callback warnings for facade callbacks exceeding slow_step_threshold.
acceptance_criteria: One test per warning/assertion triggering it with the expected message; debug off adds no measurable overhead in micro-benchmarks.

title: porto.metrics.prometheus_text() exposition
description: Render all runtime metrics (with `porto_` prefix, HELP/TYPE lines, labels like kind) in Prometheus text exposition format from `porto.metrics.prometheus_text()`.
acceptance_criteria: Output validated by `promtool check metrics` in CI; golden test for a fixed snapshot.

title: Suspended coroutine stack capture (cr_await/cr_frame walk)
description: For waiting Python tasks, build `python_stack` by walking `cr_await` chains and `cr_frame` (`f_lineno`, `co_qualname`) without executing the coroutine, under a critical section on the coroutine (3.14t safe). Handles async generators and Trap/foreign awaitables at the leaf.
acceptance_criteria: Tests on 3.11-3.14 and 3.14t: nested awaits produce the expected frame list; concurrent snapshot during heavy stepping on 3.14t is race-free under TSAN nightly.

title: aiohttp client suite >= 95% under porto
description: Drive aiohttp's client-side tests under porto to >= 95%, fixing gaps (TLS via sslproto, DNS resolver, connector limits, BufferedProtocol, timeouts). Server-side aiohttp tests are out of scope but run for information.
acceptance_criteria: compat CI reports aiohttp client tests >= 95% of baseline-passing tests.

title: httpx suite >= 95% under porto (AnyIO native backend)
description: Drive the httpx (and httpcore async) test suite under porto to >= 95% with `anyio_backend="native"`, and verify the facade fallback mode as well.
acceptance_criteria: compat CI reports httpx >= 95% of baseline-passing tests in native mode; facade mode result recorded.

title: redis.asyncio suite >= 95% under porto
description: Drive redis-py's asyncio test suite under porto to >= 95%, fixing gaps found (streams, pubsub cancellation, connection pool, asyncio.timeout usage).
acceptance_criteria: compat CI reports redis.asyncio >= 95% of baseline-passing tests.

title: asyncpg suite >= 95% under porto
description: Drive the asyncpg test suite under porto to >= 95%, fixing facade gaps found (protocol flow control, start_tls, timeouts, cancellation of in-flight queries, pool behaviour).
acceptance_criteria: compat CI reports asyncpg >= 95% of baseline-passing tests on Linux 3.12-3.14.

title: Semantic test suite for §22 rules and traceability
description: One Python test file for §22 with normative rules as test names (bridging, cancellation ack timeout, auto-hosting, sniffio, AnyIO install modes, facade restrictions), wired into the rule-ID traceability script. Include a curated subset of CPython test_asyncio run against the facade with a tracked pass list.
acceptance_criteria: Traceability report shows every MUST in §22 mapped to >= 1 test; curated test_asyncio subset runs in py-test CI on all OS legs.

title: porto.asyncio.install(), native(), run_asyncio, to_asyncio_future
description: `install()` sets the event loop policy (or on 3.14+ the loop-factory mechanism) so `asyncio.run(main())` creates a Runtime with lane 0 = this thread, facade as running loop, and `main` as a real asyncio.Task. Provide `porto.asyncio.native(coro)` to opt into Porto-native tasks, `run_asyncio(coro)` and `to_asyncio_future(awaitable)`; ship typed stubs.
acceptance_criteria: An unmodified asyncio program (streams server + client + asyncio.gather) runs under install(); porto.sleep and porto.scope usable inside it; native(coro) runs as a PyTask; pyright strict passes on typing samples.

title: AnyIO backend: task introspection and create_test_runner
description: Implement `get_current_task`, `get_running_tasks` (from the task registry), `wait_all_tasks_blocked`, and `create_test_runner` so the AnyIO pytest plugin can run tests with `anyio_backend = "porto"`.
acceptance_criteria: AnyIO's pytest plugin runs a sample suite parametrized on "porto"; wait_all_tasks_blocked test passes; get_running_tasks reports names and coroutines.

title: AnyIO backend: worker threads, from_thread, blocking portal
description: Implement `run_sync_in_worker_thread` (on porto.to_thread, abandon-on-cancel semantics), `current_default_thread_limiter` (40 tokens), `run_async_from_thread`, `run_sync_from_thread`, `create_blocking_portal` on top of `porto.from_thread` and `porto.Portal`.
acceptance_criteria: AnyIO test_to_thread / test_from_thread modules pass with backend "porto"; portal close cancels outstanding work.

title: sniffio integration: report "porto" in Porto task steps
description: Set `sniffio.thread_local.name = "porto"` during Porto task steps (cheaply: set on lane, swap only around facade callbacks); asyncio Tasks on the facade report "asyncio". Define behaviour when `anyio_backend="facade"` (Porto tasks must then report "asyncio" so AnyIO does not look for a porto backend).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: sniffio.current_async_library() is "porto" in a Porto task, "asyncio" in a facade asyncio Task, and "asyncio" in Porto tasks under anyio_backend="facade"; no import of sniffio if it is not installed.

title: Facade run_*/stop/close rules, shutdown_asyncgens
description: `run_forever`, `run_until_complete`, `stop`, `close` are valid only in `install()` mode (Porto owns the thread) and raise `RuntimeError` inside a running Porto runtime. `shutdown_asyncgens` and `shutdown_default_executor` supported and coordinated with Porto's asyncgen hooks (§11 §9).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: calling run_until_complete inside porto.run raises RuntimeError; in install mode run_forever/stop round-trips; shutdown_asyncgens finalizes pending async generators exactly once.

title: Facade add_signal_handler/remove_signal_handler
description: Implement signal handlers via `porto.signals`, running the callback through the facade callback queue; raise like asyncio for invalid signals / non-main-thread usage; coexist with Porto's own SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown handling.
acceptance_criteria: Test sending SIGUSR1 triggers the handler once; remove_signal_handler restores default; handler for SIGINT overrides Porto's default only while registered.

title: Facade subprocess_exec/subprocess_shell transports
description: Wrap `porto.process` in `asyncio.SubprocessTransport` plus pipe transports so `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec/shell` work (stdin/stdout/stderr pipes, `wait`, `returncode`, `send_signal`, `terminate`, `kill`).
acceptance_criteria: Ported CPython test_asyncio subprocess cases pass on Linux and macOS (Windows best-effort, gaps documented); no zombie processes after test run.

title: Facade getaddrinfo/getnameinfo and run_in_executor
description: `getaddrinfo`/`getnameinfo` backed by Porto DNS with asyncio-compatible result tuples; `run_in_executor(None, fn)` on the blocking pool (default executor) or the supplied executor; `set_default_executor`, `shutdown_default_executor`.
acceptance_criteria: Result format matches socket.getaddrinfo for v4/v6/AI_PASSIVE cases; run_in_executor with ThreadPoolExecutor and default; shutdown_default_executor waits for running jobs.

title: Facade create_datagram_endpoint (UDP and Unix datagram)
description: Rust `asyncio.DatagramTransport` with `sendto`, `datagram_received`, `error_received`, flow control and the standard endpoint options (`local_addr`, `remote_addr`, `reuse_port`, `allow_broadcast`, `sock=`).
acceptance_criteria: UDP echo and connected-UDP tests; error_received on ICMP port unreachable (Linux); ported CPython datagram tests pass.

title: porto-tokio-bridge: TokioBridge::run on a sidecar runtime
description: Crate `porto-tokio-bridge`, re-exported as `porto::compat::tokio`: `TokioBridge::run(fut)` runs a Tokio-requiring future on a lazily started sidecar multi-thread Tokio runtime and awaits the result from Porto. Dropping the Porto-side future aborts the Tokio task; the sidecar shuts down with the Porto runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Example using a Tokio-only crate (e.g. tokio::net or reqwest) awaited from a porto task; cancellation test proves the Tokio task is aborted; no Tokio threads remain after porto runtime shutdown; sidecar never started if unused.

title: porto-macros: #[porto::main] and #[porto::test]
description: Proc-macro crate providing `#[porto::main(lanes = N, ...)]` and `#[porto::test(...)]` that build a Runtime via Builder and run the body inside a root scope. Attribute args map 1:1 to Builder options; good spans on errors.
acceptance_criteria: trybuild pass/fail tests for valid and invalid attributes; the §A listener example compiles and runs; `#[porto::test]` used by the porto crate's own tests.

title: porto crate: time, net, io, sync, tls, fs, process, signal surface
description: Finalize and document the public Rust surface: `time::{sleep, sleep_until, timeout, interval, Instant}` (virtualizable), `net::{TcpListener, TcpStream, UdpSocket, UnixStream, UnixListener, lookup_host}`, `io::{AsyncRead, AsyncWrite, AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt, split, copy, BufReader, Interest, Ready, AsyncFd}`, `sync::{Mutex, RwLock, Semaphore, Notify, Barrier, mpsc, oneshot, broadcast, watch}`, `tls::{TlsAcceptor, TlsConnector}`, `signal`, `process`, `fs`. Fill any helpers M1 did not provide (split, copy, BufReader).
acceptance_criteria: rustdoc for every public item with examples; doctests pass; public-API snapshot (cargo-public-api) committed; Rust TCP echo + TLS echo integration tests pass on all OS legs.

title: Extension author rules: debug assertions and published guide
description: Publish the B.6 rules (Send futures, never block, no Python::attach on Rust-only lanes on GIL builds, use call_soon_py) as a docs page with the porto-pyo3 cookbook. In debug mode, assert P1 violations at ABI boundaries (py_* called from detached thread, Py objects dropped on Rust-only lanes) and report them with the offending task name.
acceptance_criteria: Docs page exists and is linked from the porto-pyo3 crate README; debug-mode tests trigger each assertion with a clear message; release builds have zero overhead (no checks compiled in).

title: ABI stability gate: layout snapshot, minor-append, multi-major export
description: CI job that compares PortoApiV1 layout against the last released snapshot and fails on any non-append change without an abi_major bump. Add the export plumbing so porto._core can export several majors (`_ABI_V1`, `_ABI_V2`) side by side, and a test that an extension built against an older minor still loads against a newer porto. Douro and other wheels check `abi_major` at import (51 §1).
acceptance_criteria: CI fails on a deliberately reordered field in a test branch; old-minor extension fixture loads and runs against current build; a dummy `_ABI_V2` export test passes alongside V1.

title: Public API freeze: stubs match runtime and §20
description: Add a CI check (mypy.stubtest-style) that every runtime public name matches its stub signature and §20, and that names not listed in §20 are underscore-private. Generate API docs from stubs.
acceptance_criteria: CI job fails on any stub/runtime or spec drift; zero allowlist entries at 1.0; API docs build from stubs.

title: process.run and kill_on_cancel semantics
description: kill_on_cancel=True: when the waiting scope is cancelled send SIGKILL (POSIX) / TerminateProcess (Windows) and reap in a shielded background task. porto.process.run(args, *, input=None, capture=True, check=False, timeout_via_scope=True) -> CompletedProcess (CalledProcessError when check).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: move_on_after around wait kills the child and it is reaped; run(check=True) raises CalledProcessError; input piped and output captured.

title: porto.process.spawn with pidfd/SIGCHLD reaping
description: porto-process: spawn(args, stdin/stdout/stderr = PIPE|DEVNULL|None, cwd, env, start_new_session, kill_on_cancel=True) returning a Process with stdin/stdout/stderr ByteStreams, await wait(), send_signal, terminate, kill, pid, returncode. Exit detection: pidfd_open + readiness on Linux >= 5.3; otherwise SIGCHLD self-pipe + waitpid(pid, WNOHANG) reaping only our own children.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: git/echo round-trip via pipes; no zombies after 1000 spawns; does not reap children started by subprocess.Popen; fallback path forced and tested on Linux; macOS CI covers SIGCHLD path.

title: porto.fs helpers: read_bytes, atomic write, stat, walk, copy
description: read_bytes (open+fstat+read+close as one blocking-pool job), read_text(encoding), write_bytes(path, data, *, atomic=False) with tmp + fsync + rename, stat, exists, mkdir(parents, exist_ok), remove, rename, listdir, walk (async iterator), copy.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: read_bytes does exactly one pool hop (counter); atomic write leaves either old or new content under kill -9 simulation; walk matches os.walk.

title: porto.fs.open async file objects on the blocking pool
description: porto-fs: `async with await porto.fs.open(path, mode, ...)` with builtins.open modes including text (encoding, newline); methods read(n=-1), readline, readinto, write, seek, tell, truncate, flush, aclose, executed as blocking-pool jobs (io_uring ops later).
acceptance_criteria: Parity tests against builtins.open for every mode; cancellation of a pending read does not corrupt the file position contract (documented); no thread hop for already-closed errors.

title: porto.tls ServerConfig, SNI resolver and atomic reload
description: ServerConfig.from_pem_files(cert_chain=, key=, alpn=), ServerConfig.with_resolver(fn) for sync SNI cert selection cached in Rust, ServerConfig.reload() atomically swapping certs for new handshakes; session tickets on by default; enable listen_tcp(tls=) and serve_tcp(tls=). Handshake runs on the stream's lane; on GIL builds with lanes > 1, Rust-only users' handshakes (Douro) run on Rust lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: SNI selects per-host cert; reload mid-traffic affects only new connections; h2/http1.1 ALPN; ticket resumption observed; Rust-lane handshake path covered with lanes=2 on GIL build.

title: porto.tls ClientConfig, TlsStream and start_tls
description: rustls in porto-net tls with aws-lc-rs provider (feature 'ring' alternative), no OpenSSL. ClientConfig.default(alpn=...) with rustls-native-certs roots and webpki-roots fallback; ClientConfig(roots=Roots.from_pem(...), client_cert=..., verify=True). TlsStream implements ByteStream (aclose sends close_notify), exposes alpn_protocol, peer_certificates(), tls_version; stream.start_tls(cfg, server_hostname=); enable connect_tcp(tls=, server_hostname=). Errors raise porto.tls.TLSError(OSError) with .reason.
acceptance_criteria: Tests against a local rustls server and a public-CA fixture: ALPN negotiated, bad hostname -> TLSError(reason), session resumption on by default; cargo deny shows no openssl-sys; build with --features ring passes.

title: Cross-lane scope, sync and channel test pass (lanes=8)
description: Run the §15 and §16 semantic suites with lanes=8 on 3.14t, adding cross-lane cases: cancel from another lane routed via inbox (C10), channel/lock handoff between lanes, PyObj moves without copy.
acceptance_criteria: Suites green with lanes=8 under the TSAN-built CPython nightly.

title: Per-lane timer wheel shards and cross-lane timer cancel
description: With lanes > 1, each lane owns the wheel shard for timers registered on it, behind the per-lane sharded mutex; cancelling or re-arming (scope deadline change) a timer from another lane is safe; idle-lane park timeout accounts only for its own shard.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with lanes=4: deadlines set from foreign lanes fire on time; TSAN clean; proptest model extended to concurrent insert/cancel.

title: Stubs for porto.net, porto.signals, porto.lowlevel, Buffer
description: Add typed modules/stubs for porto.net (TcpStream, TcpListener, UdpSocket, UnixStream, SockAddr, connect_tcp/listen_tcp/serve_tcp/resolve/bind_udp/connect_unix/listen_unix), porto.abc.ByteStream Protocol, porto.Buffer, porto.signals and porto.lowlevel.
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict green on tests/typing net samples; TcpStream and UnixStream are structurally ByteStream (static check).

title: _core.pyi stubs for run, time, scopes, sync, channels
description: Write python/porto/_core.pyi and __init__ re-exports exactly matching §20 (PEP 695 generics) for run/Runtime/RuntimeConfig/errors (implemented by the M0/M1 runtime slice), time, Scope/Task/Started, sync primitives and channel types; ship py.typed; implement __class_getitem__ so channel[int](10), Mutex[T], watch[T] etc. are subscriptable at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict passes on python/ and tests/typing/*.py samples exercising every M1 surface; tests/typing contains negative samples (reveal_type / expected errors); runtime subscripting tested.

title: Default SIGINT/SIGTERM handling (handle_signals)
description: With handle_signals=True (main thread only): SIGINT cancels the root scope with reason KeyboardInterrupt and porto.run raises KeyboardInterrupt after shutdown; SIGTERM does the same with porto.Terminated(SystemExit); a second SIGINT within graceful_timeout forces immediate exit. handle_signals=False leaves Python defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Subprocess tests: SIGINT -> exit via KeyboardInterrupt with finally blocks run; SIGTERM -> Terminated; double SIGINT exits promptly while a shielded task hangs; handle_signals=False -> Python's default KeyboardInterrupt.

title: porto.signals.receive via self-pipe on the driver
description: porto-signal: signal-hook-style self-pipe (signalfd optional) registered with the driver; no Python-level handlers installed; delivery to the receiver regardless of the OS-chosen thread. Python: `async with porto.signals.receive(*signums) as sigs: async for signum in sigs`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGUSR1) delivered to the iterator; two receivers both get the signal; leaving the context restores previous disposition; signal raised from a non-main thread still delivered.

title: TCP echo gate: 1 KiB, 100 conns vs uvloop
description: Add bench/micro TCP echo server/client for Porto and asyncio+uvloop streams (1 KiB messages, 100 connections), plus a functional echo test in the Python suite.
acceptance_criteria: Functional echo test green in CI; on the reference machine Porto >= 1.5x uvloop streams throughput (GIL build, lanes=1); result committed to bench/results. M1 exit criterion.

title: Unix domain stream sockets
description: porto.net.connect_unix(path) and listen_unix(path, *, mode=0o660) returning UnixStream (ByteStream) and a listener; Linux abstract namespace via leading "\0".
acceptance_criteria: Tests: file mode applied to the socket path; abstract socket works on Linux and is skipped elsewhere; UnixStream passes the shared ByteStream test suite.

title: UDP sockets (bind_udp, UdpSocket)
description: porto.net.bind_udp(host, port, *, reuse_port=False, broadcast=False) -> UdpSocket with send_to, recv_from (IoOp RecvFrom/SendTo), connect, send, recv, aclose.
acceptance_criteria: Loopback tests for v4/v6 datagrams, connected-mode send/recv, broadcast flag set, cancel-safe recv_from.

title: serve_tcp: one task per connection in its own scope
description: porto.net.serve_tcp(handler, host=None, port=0, *, tls=None, max_connections=None, started=None): runs forever, spawning each connection handler in its own scope; max_connections pauses accept when reached; started.set(port) supports Scope.start(). Handler errors are logged and do not kill the server.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: `port = await s.start(porto.net.serve_tcp, handler)` works; max_connections=2 keeps the 3rd client in the backlog until one closes; cancelling the outer scope closes all connections.

title: Buffered stream reads: read_exact, read_until, readline
description: Give each stream a lane-pooled internal receive buffer. Implement read_exact(n) (porto.IncompleteReadError with .partial), read_until(sep, *, limit) including sep (porto.LimitOverrunError), readline(limit), read_to_end(*, limit). Scans happen in the buffer without copying; unconsumed bytes survive cancellation (T3).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: delimiter split across many small segments; limit overrun raises LimitOverrunError; EOF mid-read_exact raises IncompleteReadError with the partial bytes; cancelling read_until mid-way and retrying returns all bytes.

title: porto.Buffer and per-lane buffer pool
description: porto.Buffer: Rust-owned growable byte buffer exposing the read/write buffer protocol, pooled per lane in size classes 4K/16K/64K/256K; bytes(buf) copies on demand. PyBufferRef wraps PyObject_GetBuffer(PyBUF_SIMPLE) and releases the view on drop, always on a Python lane (P1).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: memoryview over Buffer is writable/readable; pool reuse observable via stats; releasing a view held across a lane hop happens on a Python lane (debug assertion); leak test 100x shows zero growth.

title: loom suite for sync, channels and scopes
description: Gather loom models for Notify, Semaphore grant-vs-cancel, mpsc close races and scope cancel vs spawn under `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p porto-core --features loom`; the task-state/inbox models are owned by the scheduler slice. Wire the nightly heavy run.
acceptance_criteria: All listed models pass with default loom preemption bound in PR CI and with a raised bound in the nightly job. M1 exit criterion.

title: §16 semantic suite for sync primitives and channels
description: tests/python/porto/test_16_sync.py covering every primitive and channel method, FIFO fairness, cancel removal, grant handoff, closure rules, blocking_* thread restrictions, and runtime subscripting of generics. §16 has no rule IDs; introduce S1..Sn IDs in the spec for traceability.
acceptance_criteria: Suite green in CI on GIL and free-threaded builds; every §16 behaviour listed in the spec table has a named test. M1 exit criterion.

title: watch channel (latest value)
description: porto.watch[T](initial) and Rust sync::watch: sender updates the latest value; rx.borrow() returns current value, await rx.changed() waits for a newer version; the clearable-event replacement recommended by §16.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: changed() returns once per version even with multiple sends coalesced; borrow after close returns last value; changed() raises EndOfChannel after sender close.

title: broadcast channel with Lagged(n)
description: porto.broadcast[T](capacity) and Rust sync::broadcast: every receiver gets every message; a receiver that falls behind gets porto.Lagged with .skipped = n and resumes at the oldest retained message.

title: oneshot channel
description: porto.oneshot[T]() -> (Sender, Receiver) and Rust sync::oneshot: single value, recv raises EndOfChannel if the sender is dropped without sending, send raises BrokenResourceError if the receiver is gone.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for send/recv, dropped sender, dropped receiver, cancel-safe recv.

title: Condition and Barrier
description: porto.Condition(lock=None): wait(), wait_for(pred), notify(n), notify_all(). porto.Barrier(n): await wait() -> bool, True for exactly one leader per generation.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: wait re-acquires the lock even when cancelled; wait_for re-checks predicate; Barrier returns exactly one True per cycle and is reusable.

title: Writer-preferring RwLock
description: porto.RwLock (sync::RwLock): writer-preferring async read/write lock with read()/write() async context managers, cancel-safe waiter removal.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a waiting writer blocks new readers; cancelled writer unblocks queued readers; no starvation in a 1k-iteration stress test.

title: Semaphore and CapacityLimiter
description: porto.Semaphore(n): acquire(k=1), release(k=1), async with, available. porto.CapacityLimiter(n): semaphore plus owner tracking with per-task borrow, AnyIO-compatible API surface (borrowed_tokens, total_tokens, acquire_on_behalf_of etc. as needed by the M4 AnyIO backend).
