title: Lock and Mutex[T] with fair FIFO handoff
description: porto.Lock (sync::Mutex<()>): fair FIFO handoff, non-reentrant, async with, locked(), try_acquire() -> bool. porto.Mutex[T](value) (sync::Mutex<PyObj>): `async with m as v` yields a guard exposing the value and v.set(new).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: FIFO acquisition order under contention; re-entrant acquire deadlocks are detected by a test with timeout (documented non-reentrant); cancelled waiter does not leak the lock; Mutex[int] subscriptable at runtime.

title: §15 semantic suite and Trio cancel-scope test port
description: Collect tests/python/porto/test_15_scopes.py with one test per rule (C1-C12, start protocol, task cancel, exceptions table) and port the relevant subset of Trio's cancel-scope and nursery tests (license-compatible) to the Porto API. Register rule IDs for the traceability-matrix script.
acceptance_criteria: All C1-C12 rule IDs have >= 1 passing test; ported Trio subset passes; suite runs in CI on GIL and free-threaded builds (lanes=1). This is an M1 exit criterion.

title: Scope object surface: cancel, properties, tasks snapshot
description: Finalize the Python Scope class per §20: porto.scope(*, timeout, deadline, shield, name, raise_on_timeout); Scope.spawn(coro_or_fn, *args, name, pin, context) (pin accepted, enforced in M2); cancel(reason); deadline/shield read-write; cancel_called, cancelled_caught, timed_out, name, tasks (live children snapshot); porto.current_task().
acceptance_criteria: Python tests per attribute; a signature test compares inspect.signature of every Scope member against §20.

title: Task.cancel() via implicit per-task scope
description: Wrap each spawned task's coroutine in an implicit per-task scope; Task.cancel() cancels that scope only. The absorbed Cancelled does not count as a failure of the parent and does not cancel siblings; Task.cancelled() reports True and Task.result() raises accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: cancelling one child leaves siblings running and the parent scope exits cleanly; task.cancelled() is True; cancel on a done task is a no-op.

title: Scope.start() and the Started[T] protocol
description: Implement `await s.start(fn, *args, name=None)`: spawn with started=Started() injected as kwarg into a hidden scope owned by the caller, return the value passed to started.set(v), then re-parent the task into s (Trio nursery.start semantics). Exceptions before set propagate to the caller of start; started.set twice raises RuntimeError.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: start returns the set value; exception before set raised from start (not as group of s); after set, a failure is reported by s; cancel of caller before set cancels the child; double set raises RuntimeError.

title: Shield scopes and sync-with shield-only usage (C8)
description: porto.shield(*, timeout=None) == porto.scope(shield=True, ...). A scope entered with sync `with` is shield-only: spawn/start raise RuntimeError. Scope.shield is read/write and changing it re-evaluates effective cancellation of tasks in the subtree.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic tests test_C8_shield_blocks_outer_cancel, test_C8_shield_own_cancel_counts, test_C8_sync_with_cannot_spawn, test_C8_shield_timeout_in_finally (ST-9 rollback pattern).

title: loom models: wake/steal/inbox races
description: loom models with 3 lanes and 3 tasks covering wake vs steal, inbox push vs park, injector vs LIFO slot, idle-set unpark races.
acceptance_criteria: loom suite green in the nightly heavy run.

title: Scheduler property, fairness and starvation tests
description: Property test (proptest, random spawn/wake/steal schedules) that no task is ever polled concurrently by two lanes; multi-lane fairness (injector progress within 2 x global_queue_interval) and LIFO ping-pong starvation tests.
acceptance_criteria: All tests green on lanes 1, 2, 8 for 10k iterations in CI.

title: Multi-lane shutdown and drain
description: Extend shutdown to N lanes: Shared.shutdown flag, each lane finishes current task, drains (drop Rust tasks, cancel Python tasks with 2 s budget on a Python lane), lanes join, then driver closes; Python tasks queued on Rust lanes routed to a Python lane for cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: shutdown under load with lanes=8 leaves no live tasks, threads, or FDs; Python finally blocks run.

title: GIL-degraded mode on free-threaded builds
description: Install sys.meta_path finder wrapper at start; after each extension import check sys._is_gil_enabled() (cached). On flip: Shared.degraded = true (one-way), lanes 1..N-1 stop accepting Python tasks and hand them to lane 0's inbox at their next scheduling point, log once 'porto: GIL was re-enabled by importing <module>; ...'.
acceptance_criteria: Test on 3.14t: importing a fixture extension without Py_mod_gil mid-run degrades, all Python tasks subsequently run on lane 0, warning names the module exactly once, Rust tasks still use all lanes.

title: Python task steal policy, threshold and pinning
description: Python tasks stealable only if not PIN and victim queue >= python_steal_threshold (8); python_steal='off' disables migration globally; pin=True honoured (subtree inheritance resolved via scope inheritance).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: pinned task always runs on its spawn lane under heavy load; light load (< threshold) causes no migration; python_steal='off' never migrates.

title: Rust-only lanes on GIL builds and py_injector
description: GIL build lanes>1: lanes 1..N-1 are RustOnly and never attach. run(t) of a Python task on a Rust lane pushes to py_injector and unparks lane 0; lane 0 drains py_injector. porto.lowlevel.spawn_rust_lane(fn) / spawn_rust for Rust-heavy offload (TLS handshakes, compression). Rust lanes never drop Python refs (PyDeferred only).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: Rust-only work proceeds on lanes 1..N-1 while lane 0 runs Python; Python task woken from Rust lane runs on lane 0; debug assertion catches Python drop on Rust lane.

title: Driver ownership across lanes (driver_lock)
description: At most one parked lane owns the driver via driver_lock TryLock and blocks in it with next-timer timeout; others park on futex. unpark(lane) wakes the driver waker if that lane owns it, else futex. Maintenance polls driver non-blocking only if no lane is blocked in it.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: I/O readiness wakes a task while all lanes are parked; no two lanes inside driver turn simultaneously (assert); timers fire on time with N lanes.

title: IdleSet, searching state and unpark policy
description: Tokio-style idle algorithm: bitset of parked lanes + num_searching; bounded searchers (at most lanes/2); a searching lane that finds work wakes another if needed; avoid thundering herd.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: N idle lanes with one wake -> exactly one unpark; no lost wakeup under 10M random wake/park iterations.

title: LIFO slot with starvation cap
description: Same-lane wake while running a task goes to lifo_slot, displacing previous occupant to local queue; max 3 consecutive LIFO runs then force local queue; budget-exhausted tasks never use the LIFO slot.
acceptance_criteria: Starvation test: LIFO ping-pong pair does not starve a third task; microbench shows reduced cross-lane ping-pong latency.

title: Remote inbox and soft affinity for cross-lane wakes
description: Per-lane SegQueue inbox consumed at the start of next_task. Wake from another lane/foreign thread: owner_lane idle -> push to its inbox and unpark; else injector + unpark one idle lane if num_searching == 0. owner_lane updated on each run.
acceptance_criteria: Test: task woken from foreign thread runs on its owner lane when idle (owner_lane check); loom model in m2-loom-scheduler.

title: GATE: task-layer micro-benchmarks (§11 table, §53 spawn/switch)
description: Port the M0 suite to the production core and add CI regression tracking: checkpoint <= 60 ns, Yield switch <= 250 ns, spawn+complete <= 900 ns, asyncio+uvloop create_task+await >= 2.5x slower; spawn+join 100k >= 3x; yield ping-pong >= 2.5x. Oneshot <= 600 ns, channel/Lock/sleep/TCP rows are gated by their owners.
acceptance_criteria: Results JSON in bench/results/ on reference machine all green; CI perf job fails on >10% regression.

title: porto.to_thread with context copy, cancellable and limiter
description: async to_thread(fn, *args, cancellable=False, limiter=None, **kw): runs in a copy of the caller context; default shields until the thread finishes; cancellable=True raises Cancelled immediately and discards the late result; default limiter porto.to_thread.default_limiter() with 40 tokens (CapacityLimiter from sync work).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: contextvar visible in fn and not leaked back; cancel with cancellable=False waits for completion; cancellable=True returns immediately; 41st concurrent call waits on the limiter.

title: Elastic blocking pool and spawn_blocking
description: Elastic pool up to blocking_threads (512), idle exit after blocking_keepalive (10 s); jobs FnOnce + Send or Python callables; Python jobs attach via a per-thread PyThreadState kept for the thread lifetime and detach after. porto::task::spawn_blocking -> JoinHandle<R>; no block_in_place. Shutdown waits <= 1 s then detaches.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: grows under 100 concurrent jobs and shrinks after keepalive (virtual time or short keepalive); Python job sees attached state; results/exceptions propagate.

title: Per-lane intrusive task registry and snapshot handshake
description: Link every task (Rust and Python) into its lane's intrusive list on spawn, unlink on completion, lock-free on the hot path. Snapshot request posted to each lane, copied at next maintenance tick (or immediately if idle). Produces raw records for TaskInfo; porto.inspect API itself is M5.
acceptance_criteria: Test: 10k live tasks snapshot returns exactly the live set; spawn/complete throughput regression < 3% vs registry disabled.

title: Shutdown sequence: DRAINING, CANCELLING, abandon, STOPPED
description: Runtime.shutdown(timeout) and signal-triggered drain: porto.lifecycle.shutdown_requested() event, graceful_timeout for main, cancel root scope (reason Shutdown) with cancel_timeout, abandon survivors by coroutine close() (drop + warning with names and stacks if close awaits), then close asyncgens, blocking pool (<= 1 s then detach), driver, join lanes. Scheduler drains remaining Rust tasks by drop and Python tasks by Cancelled with 2 s budget. Needs scopes and Event from other M1 work.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: main finishing within graceful_timeout returns normally; stuck task abandoned after cancel_timeout with warning listing it; no leaked threads/FDs after run returns (leak test).

title: porto.errors hierarchy and Rust error chain notes
description: Define PortoError and subclasses (NoRuntimeError, RuntimeClosed, WouldBlock, EndOfChannel, BrokenResourceError, ClosedResourceError, IncompleteReadError.partial, LimitOverrunError, Lagged.skipped, InvalidStateError, RustPanic.message), Cancelled(asyncio.CancelledError), Terminated(SystemExit), re-exported at top level with .pyi stubs. Rust->Python conversion attaches __notes__ 'caused by: ...' for the error chain.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: MRO/isinstance of each class matches §20; a Rust error with 3-level source chain produces 3 notes; stubs pass pyright strict.

title: RuntimeConfig, env PORTO_* parsing and precedence
description: Frozen RuntimeConfig dataclass with all §20 fields; precedence explicit overrides > RuntimeConfig > PORTO_* env > defaults; env parsing of ints, floats, bools (1/0/true/false/yes/no), enums by lowercase name; unknown PORTO_* vars warn with valid names. Validation (lanes >= 1 or 'auto'; 'auto' = physical cores capped 64, GIL builds min(2, cores)). Rust Builder mirrors the same fields.
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven tests for precedence, each parse type, invalid values error clearly, typo warning lists valid names, 'auto' resolution on GIL vs free-threaded.

title: Panic policy: RustPanic in tasks, abort in scheduler
description: catch_unwind at every #[pymethods] and ABI entry point and around task poll; panic inside a task fails it with porto.RustPanic (message + location); panic in scheduler internals logs and aborts. Enforce panic=unwind in profiles (build check).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: panicking Rust future -> RustPanic propagated into scope, lane keeps running; subprocess test that a scheduler-internal panic aborts.

title: porto.Task handle, current_task and lowlevel trap API
description: Lazily created porto.Task[T] holding TaskRef: id, name, done, cancelled, result (InvalidStateError if not done), exception, cancel, __await__ -> TrapKind::Join or ready path, lane, pinned. porto.current_task(); porto.lowlevel.trap_yield(), trap_wait_notify(), current_lane(). Internal spawns never create the handle. Task.cancel delegates to the scope module.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for each method incl. awaiting a completed task (no trap), awaiting a failed task re-raises; internal spawn creates no Python handle (counter).

title: loom models for task state machine
description: loom model tests (cfg loom) for wake-during-poll, wake-after-complete, concurrent cancel+wake, and drop-of-last-waker over the harness.
acceptance_criteria: `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p porto-core --features loom` green with all four models.

title: Spike: profile and tune hot path to §11 targets
description: Profile (perf, py-spy native) the step loop, trap and ready paths; remove INCREF/DECREF pairs (steal semantics into PyIter_Send), ensure no per-await allocation on ready path, check task switch path. Time-boxed to the remainder of the 2-3 week spike.
acceptance_criteria: Flame graphs and before/after numbers attached to the gate issue.

title: Decisions: ADRs, open questions and spec conflicts
description: Decisions that block work (license, MSRV, docs toolchain, benchmark gates, reference machine) and the open questions from 55 §2, deferred until evidence arrives.
acceptance_criteria: Every decision recorded as an ADR in 04-decision-records.md or closed with its default.

title: M3 — ABI and Rust facade
description: porto-abi v1, porto-pyo3, the porto crate API, hyper compat, tokio bridge. Also TLS, fs and process, and the name check before anything is published.
acceptance_criteria: A sample PyO3 extension in examples/ doing TCP through the ABI passes its tests; the hyper client example works.

title: M2 — Multi-lane and free-threaded scaling
description: Lanes, work stealing, inbox, LIFO slot, free-threaded attach policy, GIL-degraded mode, Rust lanes on GIL builds.
acceptance_criteria: Free-threaded scaling gates; TSAN clean.

title: M1 — Core runtime (single lane)
description: porto-core complete on one lane: scopes (full §15), timer wheel, sync primitives, channels, budget, registry; porto-io on epoll/kqueue; TCP/UDP/Unix; DNS; blocking pool; signals; errors, config and lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: §15/§16 semantic tests green; TCP echo gate; loom suite green.

title: Follow-ups from the workspace PR (#3)
description: 1) Published crates (porto, porto-abi, porto-pyo3) move rust-version to pin minus two (ADR-031) in M3. 2) porto-py doesn't enable pyo3 extension-module; maturin packaging (hk-python-packaging) must handle linking. 3) Declare the module's GIL usage explicitly (gil_used = false) and test on 3.14t when real bindings land. 4) cargo picked the default python3 = Homebrew 3.15.2; CI and maturin must pin PYO3_PYTHON per matrix leg.
acceptance_criteria: Each item handled in the bead that owns it, or noted there.
notes:
From #4: (5) sdist not built yet: it needs crates/ and python/ from above packaging/porto (the include entries are wheel-only) — handle in the release workflow bead. (6) Note the maturin include workaround for python-source outside the pyproject dir in 50-repository-layout.md.
From #5: (7) license symlinks in packaging/porto break on Windows checkouts with core.symlinks=false; verify in the Windows CI leg, fallback = copies + equality check.

title: Support CPython 3.15 (released) alongside the 3.11-3.14 targets
description: The spec targets CPython 3.11-3.14 and 3.14t, but 3.15 is out (3.15.2 installed here; uv offers 3.15 free-threaded). Default: add 3.15 and 3.15t to the wheel and test matrices from M1, and rerun the trap-protocol checks against 3.15 coroutine internals.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-024, NG3 and 51 §1 updated; m1-ci-py-matrix includes 3.15/3.15t.

title: GATE: 8 lanes vs N asyncio loops on HTTP JSON (53 §3)
description: The free-threaded work-stealing gate includes an HTTP JSON case, which needs an HTTP app. m2-vs-asyncio-loops-gate covers TCP echo and skewed load; this reruns the HTTP variant on Douro or the raw porto HTTP baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Porto with 8 lanes >= 1.3x N asyncio loops on HTTP JSON on the reference machine.

title: Spec errata: Douro wording and milestone conflicts
description: Layer ABI is M8 in §35 but M9+ in the roadmap (planned as m8-layer-abi-spec + m9-layer-abi); cancel_after vs douro.CancelAfter; §36 says 'schema engine' where it means oxiform; §40 max_queue_wait queue is not described in §31; confirm problem 'type' URIs for the 422 body; decide whether OX-6 is P0 for M6 (planned as a hard dependency of m6-http-gates).
acceptance_criteria: Douro chapters and the roadmap agree.

title: Spec errata: runtime API gaps found while planning
description: Fix in the spec before the stubs freeze: gil_switch_interval missing from RuntimeConfig; spawn_rust vs lowlevel.spawn_rust_lane naming; pin inheritance has no API (pin: bool | None?); auto lane cap 64 (§12) vs 16 (ADR-025, Douro); §20 lacks RwLock methods, Mutex guard type, CapacityLimiter AnyIO set, UdpSocket/UnixListener classes, send_fds/recv_fds, Buffer methods; §16 has no rule IDs (add S1..Sn); §15 C10 does not list non-cancellable traps; §14 does not say which wheel shard owns a stolen task's timer; connect_tcp tls=False vs listen_tcp tls=None; trace_tasks, porto.metrics, porto.tracing, testing.explore and allow_real_io missing from §20.
acceptance_criteria: Each item fixed in the spec or recorded as a decision; §20 is complete enough for exact stubs.

title: io_uring py-test leg on a privileged Linux runner
description: Add a py-test leg on a Linux >= 5.19 runner where io_uring is permitted (self-hosted or VM, since containers often block it) running the suite with io_backend="io_uring" and io_backend_strict, plus a test that the fallback to epoll warns when io_uring_setup returns EPERM (seccomp profile).
acceptance_criteria: io_uring leg green; strict mode proven to use io_uring (backend reported by porto.inspect); fallback test green under a seccomp deny profile.

title: Assign the io_uring backend to a milestone
description: The roadmap lists epoll/kqueue in M1 but never schedules the opt-in io_uring backend, while CI expects a privileged io_uring runner. Current default: io_uring backend in M8 (opt-in, not on the 1.0 critical path) with its CI leg (m8-ci-io-uring) landing together.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone recorded in 54-roadmap.md; the backend issue and m8-ci-io-uring moved there if different.

title: PGO dist profile for release wheels
description: Build porto-py and douro-py with -Cprofile-generate under the dist profile, train on bench/http JSON and plaintext scenarios and the bench/micro task benchmarks, merge with llvm-profdata, and rebuild with -Cprofile-use. Wire into the release wheel builds only (cargo-pgo or a script per platform where training can run natively; skip PGO where it cannot and record it). Measure the gain on the reference machine.
acceptance_criteria: Release builds use merged profiles on Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS arm64; perf results show the PGO delta; non-release builds are unaffected.

title: Fuzz targets for the multipart parser and WebSocket codec
description: Add cargo-fuzz targets for the multipart parser (limits respected, safe_filename never contains path separators or '..') and the WebSocket frame codec (masking, fragmentation, control frame rules, max message size), wired into the PR smoke and nightly fuzz jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Both targets run in the nightly job; invariant assertions present; seed corpora from the conformance suites committed.

title: cargo-fuzz targets for router normalization and request head
description: fuzz/ crate with cargo-fuzz targets for douro-router path normalization (invariants: idempotent, never escapes root, no panic) and the HTTP request head through hyper plus Douro's head checks (TE+CL rejection, duplicate CL, obs-fold per §40). PRs touching douro crates run each target 60 s; a nightly job runs 30 min per target with a persisted corpus. The JSON lexer+validator target belongs to oxiform and is tracked there.
acceptance_criteria: Targets build on nightly; PR smoke and nightly jobs green; crashes are uploaded as artifacts and minimized inputs become regression tests.

title: AnyIO version matrix for the native backend
description: Weekly job running the AnyIO backend tests against the supported AnyIO version range and AnyIO main, verifying the version gate: supported versions use the native backend, unknown versions fall back to the facade with a warning.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix green for supported versions; AnyIO main failures open a tracking issue; the fallback path is exercised in at least one leg.

title: Release workflow for 0.x porto prereleases (trusted publishing)
description: release.yml modelled on kinemo: tag vX.Y.Z; preflight checks the tag matches the package version, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md is current and towncrier builds; maturin-action builds porto wheels for the tier-1 subset (manylinux_2_28 x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, Windows x86_64; 3.11-3.14) plus sdist; each wheel is installed on a clean runner and runs a smoke program; publish to PyPI through Trusted Publishing (no token) and create the GitHub release with this version's changelog section. workflow_dispatch builds without publishing.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run builds and smoke-tests every wheel; a tag on TestPyPI publishes via OIDC; a mismatched tag fails preflight.

title: Leak test harness and nightly leak job
description: pytest plugin option --leak-check that reruns each selected test 100x after warmup, sampling tracemalloc object counts, RSS and open FD count (psutil or /proc/self/fd), and fails on any object growth or FD growth. Tests mark exemptions explicitly with a reason. A nightly job runs it over the porto suite on Linux and macOS.
acceptance_criteria: A test that leaks one socket or one object per run is reported with its growth numbers; the nightly job is green on the M1 suite.

title: Nightly TSAN/ASAN job for porto-core
description: Scheduled job on nightly Rust with -Zsanitizer=thread and -Zsanitizer=address plus -Zbuild-std for porto-core and porto-io tests on Linux x86_64. TSAN suppressions file kept empty by default; any entry needs a comment. The free-threaded CPython TSAN leg is m2-ci-tsan-cpython.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly TSAN and ASAN runs green; an injected data race in a test fails TSAN; suppressions file is empty or justified.

title: Nightly CI against CPython main
description: Scheduled job building porto-py against the CPython development branch (setup-python 3.x-dev or a cached source build) and running the Python suite, to catch changes in am_send/PyIter_Send behavior early. Failures open or update a tracking issue instead of blocking PRs.
acceptance_criteria: The nightly run appears in Actions; a forced failure opens a labelled issue; the job is not a required check.

title: Fill the CLAUDE.md project section; tidy AGENTS.md
description: Replace the placeholders in CLAUDE.md: Build & Test (the CONTRIBUTING command list, maturin develop -m packaging/porto/pyproject.toml, nextest, how to run loom/deterministic suites once they exist); Architecture Overview (crate map from §50, single runtime owned by porto._core and reached only through porto-abi (ADR-004), trap protocol (ADR-001), lanes (ADR-003), Douro one crossing per request (ADR-018), oxiform for schemas (ADR-019)); Conventions (spec is normative, cite §/rule IDs in code and tests, every MUST gets a test, ADR changes go through 04-decision-records, no borrowed-ref C APIs, SAFETY comments, English). AGENTS.md has the beads block three times: keep one.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md has no '_Add your..._' placeholders; commands in it run; AGENTS.md has a single beads block.

title: Spec rule traceability matrix script
description: scripts/spec_trace.py extracts normative rule IDs (bold IDs like C1..C11, T1, I1..I4, P0..P3) and MUST/SHOULD sentences per spec file, and greps test names (Rust and Python) for them. Rule IDs repeat across files (P0..P3, T1), so IDs are file-qualified (e.g. 15.C4) and tests mark them via name plus a marker or doc comment. Emits docs/traceability.md and a JSON summary; CI runs it informationally from M1 and as a gate in M8.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script on the spec lists every rule ID with its tests or 'uncovered'; a fixture test with test_C4_* is counted for 15.C4; CI uploads the matrix as an artifact.

title: Docs site skeleton with strict build and Pages deploy
description: Docs site per the chosen toolchain (spec says mkdocs-material; kinemo instead generates Markdown from code and builds a SvelteKit site, see dec-docs-toolchain). Navigation: Home, Guides (porto, douro), API (generated from .pyi stubs, wired in M7), Cookbook, Design (docs/spec rendered as-is). CI builds in strict mode (broken links fail) and a website.yml workflow deploys main to GitHub Pages. Add a link checker for README and docs like kinemo's test_doc_links.py.
acceptance_criteria: Strict docs build passes in CI and fails on a broken relative link or anchor; Pages serves the site from main.
notes: ADR-032: Zensical + mkdocstrings-python (API from .pyi stubs); keep the config mkdocs.yml-compatible so mkdocs-material 9.x is a drop-in fallback.
spec_id: docs/spec/50-engineering/50-repository-layout.md (docs/: mkdocs-material; guides, API generated from stubs, cookbook)

title: CHANGELOG with towncrier fragments
description: CHANGELOG.md with kinemo's header (SemVer; 0.x minors may break the API until 1.0) and an Unreleased section. [tool.towncrier] in the root pyproject: directory changes/, fragment types added/changed/deprecated/removed/fixed/security, template rendering kinemo's '**Added**' headings, one changelog for porto and douro with a component prefix. CI job: a PR touching crates/ or python/ needs a fragment unless labelled skip-changelog.
acceptance_criteria: towncrier build --draft renders the fragments in kinemo's style; the fragment check fails a PR without one and passes with the label.

title: Issue and PR templates, dependabot
description: ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml (smallest program that shows it; what happens vs expected with traceback; environment: python -VV, GIL or free-threaded, porto/douro versions, OS, io_backend; a seed when porto.testing reproduces it), feature_request.yml (what you want to write, how you do it today, proposed API), config.yml (blank issues off; Discussions, docs, security policy links). PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md with 'What and why' and the checks list from CONTRIBUTING plus 'spec section / rule IDs touched' and 'changelog fragment added'. dependabot.yml for github-actions, cargo and pip (weekly, grouped).
acceptance_criteria: New issue page shows the two forms and the contact links; a test PR shows the template; dependabot opens its first grouped PR.

title: Benchmarks: SSE fan-out, WS echo, 20-query DB
description: Add remaining scenarios to bench/http: SSE fan-out 10k clients, WS echo, 20-query DB with mock driver latency 0.2 ms; competitor apps for each.
acceptance_criteria: Scenarios reproducible via the harness; results published with machine info.

title: Test client sim transport and deterministic mode
description: Client transport "sim" over porto.testing.net and Client(app, deterministic=True, seed=) running under porto.testing so failures replay by seed.
acceptance_criteria: Same test suite passes on sim transport; a seeded race reproduces 100% across reruns.

title: douro check linter
description: douro check freezes the app and lints: blocking calls in inline=True handlers, awaits in finally without a shield (AST heuristic), missing annotations; non-zero exit on errors.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture apps produce the expected diagnostics and exit codes.

title: Windows supervisor spawn mode with WSADuplicateSocket
description: Windows workers spawned (no fork) with listener sockets shared via WSADuplicateSocket; signals mapped to console control events.
acceptance_criteria: Windows CI runs multi-worker e2e and graceful stop.

title: --preload: import once then fork workers
description: With --preload import the app in the supervisor and fork() workers, asserting no non-main threads and no runtime exist before forking; mutually exclusive with --reload.
acceptance_criteria: Test: preload works; a preloaded app that starts a thread fails fast with a clear error.

title: Docs UIs: Scalar, Redoc, Swagger and offline assets
description: docs_url=/docs (Scalar default), redoc_url and swagger_url opt-in, assets from a pinned CDN URL; douro[docs-offline] extra vendors assets into the wheel with licenses.
acceptance_criteria: Pages render in a headless browser smoke test online and with docs-offline installed.

title: douro.JSONStream[T] (buffered until OX-7)
description: Async iteration over items of a top-level JSON array validated as T. Stopgap: buffer the body within limits and iterate decoded items; switch to OX-7 push decoding when released.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for valid/invalid items and limit enforcement; follow-up switch noted when ext-ox7 lands.

title: StaticFiles Rust-native mount
description: app.mount("/static", douro.StaticFiles(dir)) served entirely in Rust using the file response machinery; follow_symlinks=False default; index/404 handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: served without Python crossing, traversal and symlink escapes rejected.

title: JwtVerify layer with JWKS
description: JwtVerify(jwks_url, issuer, audience, algorithms=[RS256, ES256], required) verifies tokens in Rust, caches/refreshes JWKS, exposes claims lazily as request.auth; 401 problem when required and missing/invalid.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with generated keys: valid, expired, wrong aud/iss, alg not allowed, JWKS rotation.

title: RateLimit layer (GCRA, memory and Redis stores)
description: RateLimit(key=ip|header:<name>|rust expr, rate="100/minute", burst) using GCRA; per-worker memory store and shared Redis store via a Rust client on porto-abi I/O; 429 problem with Retry-After.
acceptance_criteria: GCRA unit tests under virtual time; Redis store integration test; 429 responses carry Retry-After.

title: Pydantic model adapter (stopgap until oxiform shim)
description: Accept pydantic models as body/return types through Douro's adapter: decode via __pydantic_validator__.validate_json, encode via the model's JSON serializer restricted to the declared type, map pydantic errors into the combined 422 shape. Removed once oxiform 1.2 ships its pydantic shim.
acceptance_criteria: Pydantic body/response tests including 422 shape parity with oxiform errors.

title: OX-9: per-call unknown= override
description: oxiform should accept unknown="forbid"|"ignore" per decode call, overriding the model option, so Douro can offer App(unknown="forbid") for request bodies globally.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform test: model with unknown=ignore rejects extra keys when decoded with per-call forbid; available via OX-1.

title: OX-7: push/incremental decoding over chunks
description: oxiform should accept non-contiguous chunked input and stream top-level array items, enabling douro.JSONStream[T] without buffering. Until then Douro buffers the body (limits apply).
acceptance_criteria: oxiform test: array split across arbitrary chunk boundaries yields the same items as contiguous decode; exposed via OX-1.

title: Stopgap: link oxiform-py as rlib with exact version pin
description: Documented fallback if OX-1..OX-5 are not released when Douro M6 starts: link oxiform-py as an rlib with an exact version pin (=X.Y.Z) and call its Rust API directly, accepting a duplicate plan cache temporarily. Decide go/no-go at M6 kickoff based on oxiform status and define the removal path once OX-1 lands.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (ADR note) with trigger date; if adopted, douro builds against the pinned rlib and a follow-up issue tracks the switch to OX-1.

title: Guides: observability and deterministic testing
description: Guide pages for inspect/dump, watchdog tuning, metrics (Prometheus/OTel), console, debug mode, and deterministic testing (testing.run, sim network, explore, pytest plugin, reproducing with PORTO_SEED).
acceptance_criteria: Pages build; examples executed in CI.

title: OpenTelemetry metrics exporter (porto[otel] extra)
description: Optional `porto[otel]` extra registering observable instruments for every runtime metric with an OpenTelemetry MeterProvider. No import cost when the extra is not installed.
acceptance_criteria: Test with the OTel in-memory metric reader sees all metrics; `import porto` does not import opentelemetry.

title: porto.tracing: OTel spans per task (trace_tasks)
description: `porto.tracing` integrates with OpenTelemetry if installed: with `trace_tasks=True` each spawned task creates a span linked to the parent span via contextvars (copied on spawn). Add `trace_tasks` to RuntimeConfig (missing from §20 table).
acceptance_criteria: In-memory span exporter test shows parent/child task spans with correct links and task names; no spans and no overhead when trace_tasks=False.

title: Compat guide: using asyncio/AnyIO libraries under Porto
description: Guide covering goals and limits, install() for gradual adoption, bridging cost, CancelledError semantics difference (§15 §5), anyio_backend modes, and the published compat pass-rate table.
acceptance_criteria: Page builds; examples run in CI; pass-rate table generated from the compat job artifact.

title: Rust API guide: porting from Tokio, porto-pyo3 cookbook
description: Guide pages: porto crate quickstart, Tokio-to-Porto name mapping and differences (spawn requires a scope, no block_in_place), when to use TokioBridge, hyper compat, and a porto-pyo3 cookbook built from the examples.
acceptance_criteria: Pages build in mkdocs; every code block is compiled as a doctest or example in CI.

title: porto::compat::futures_io adapters
description: Adapters converting between porto `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite` and `futures::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncWrite}` in both directions (wrapper types plus extension traits).
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip tests with `futures::io::copy` over a porto TcpStream; vectored write forwarding tested.

title: Windows IOCP backend (mio AFD) and Windows net/process/signal
description: Enable the mio IOCP/AFD backend as Windows default, gate Unix-only APIs (Unix sockets abstract namespace, SCM_RIGHTS, pidfd), Windows process exit via handles and TerminateProcess, and Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Break mapping for handle_signals.
acceptance_criteria: Windows CI runs the net, process and signal suites (Unix-only tests skipped); wheels built for win_amd64 in the M8 wheel matrix.

title: io_uring readiness backend with probe and fallback
description: Opt-in io_backend='io_uring' (Linux >= 5.19): probe io_uring_setup(256) with SINGLE_ISSUER|DEFER_TASKRUN when available; on EPERM/ENOSYS/EINVAL or RLIMIT_MEMLOCK failure fall back to epoll with a warning unless io_backend_strict. One ring per lane (single issuer). Readiness via IORING_OP_POLL_ADD multishot mapped into the same ScheduledIo bits.
acceptance_criteria: Full M1 net/IO test suite passes with io_backend='io_uring'; fallback tested in a seccomp/Docker profile denying io_uring; strict mode raises.

title: Stubs for porto.inspect and porto.testing
description: Typed surface for porto.inspect (tasks() -> list[TaskInfo], tree() -> ScopeInfo, stats() -> RuntimeStats, dump) and porto.testing (run(main, *, seed, clock, autojump, network, **cfg), Clock, net.Network, net.Link, pytest plugin fixtures). Implementations owned by the M5 slice.
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict green on tests/typing samples for inspect and testing.

title: Stubs for porto.asyncio compat module
description: Typed surface for porto.asyncio: EventLoop (asyncio.AbstractEventLoop subclass), install(), run_asyncio(coro), to_asyncio_future(awaitable). Implementation is owned by the M4 compat slice.
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict green on tests/typing asyncio samples.

title: Stubs for porto.tls, porto.fs, porto.process
description: Typed modules/stubs for porto.tls (ClientConfig, ServerConfig, Roots, TlsStream, TLSError), porto.fs (open overloads by mode returning text/binary file types, helpers, Path) and porto.process (spawn, Process, run, CompletedProcess, PIPE/DEVNULL).
acceptance_criteria: pyright --strict green on tests/typing samples; fs.open overloads reveal str vs bytes return types correctly.

title: porto.fs.Path async pathlib mirror
description: porto.fs.Path wrapping pathlib.Path: I/O methods (read_bytes, read_text, write_*, stat, exists, iterdir, mkdir, unlink, open, ...) are async and use porto.fs; pure methods and operators delegate to pathlib returning porto.fs.Path.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: each pathlib I/O method has an async counterpart with identical results; `/` and with_suffix return porto.fs.Path.

title: UnixStream send_fds/recv_fds (SCM_RIGHTS)
description: UnixStream.send_fds(data, fds) and recv_fds(max, maxfds) using SCM_RIGHTS; received FDs are CLOEXEC.
acceptance_criteria: Test passes a pipe FD across a socketpair and reads through it; truncation flag surfaced.

title: Stream sendfile with OS zero-copy and fallback
description: await stream.sendfile(file, offset=0, count=None): sendfile(2) on Linux, sendfile on macOS, read/write fallback elsewhere or for non-regular files; respects backpressure and cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: 10 MiB file transferred byte-exact with offset/count variants; fallback path covered by forcing it; cancellation mid-transfer leaves stream usable state documented.

title: porto.lowlevel readiness API for foreign FDs
description: Expose porto.lowlevel.wait_readable(fileobj_or_fd), wait_writable(...), notify_closing(fd) and current_driver_kind() using IoOp::WaitReadable/WaitWritable. notify_closing wakes waiters with ClosedResourceError. (trap_yield, trap_wait_notify, current_lane, spawn_rust_lane belong to the task-model/scheduler slices.)
acceptance_criteria: Test integrating a raw socket.socket(): wait_readable completes when data arrives; notify_closing wakes a waiter with ClosedResourceError; current_driver_kind() returns 'epoll' or 'kqueue'.

title: Micro benchmarks: channel, Lock, sleep vs asyncio
description: Add pyperf scripts in bench/micro for channel ping-pong (bounded 1) vs asyncio.Queue, Lock contention with 100 tasks, and sleep(0.001) x 100k tasks, plus criterion benches for wheel insert/cancel and channel push/pop.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks run in CI (trend only) and on the reference machine; record results in bench/results. Targets: channel >= 3x, Lock >= 2x, timers >= 2x vs asyncio+uvloop; misses filed as perf bugs (hard gate at M8).

title: Cancelled type, swallow detection, foreign CancelledError (C11)
description: porto.Cancelled subclasses asyncio.CancelledError. In debug mode warn 'cancellation was swallowed' when a task finishes normally after Cancelled was delivered inside an effectively cancelled scope. asyncio.CancelledError raised by user/asyncio code while the Porto scope is not cancelled is treated as a regular failure. Awaiting a Porto awaitable outside a runtime raises porto.NoRuntimeError.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: isinstance(Cancelled(), asyncio.CancelledError); debug=True emits the swallow warning exactly once; foreign CancelledError appears in the scope's ExceptionGroup; await porto.sleep(0) without runtime raises NoRuntimeError.

title: porto.interval with burst/skip/delay missed-tick modes
description: Implement porto.interval(period, *, missed='skip') -> AsyncIterator[float] yielding the scheduled tick time, following Tokio MissedTickBehavior semantics for 'burst', 'skip' and 'delay'.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with a stalled consumer (blocking step longer than 3 periods) assert the yielded tick sequence for each mode matches Tokio's documented behaviour; invalid missed value raises ValueError.

title: GATE: 1M sleeping tasks RSS < 2.5 GB, spawn >= 1M/s/lane
description: Benchmark spawning 1M tasks that each sleep (embedded timer entry, no per-task allocation beyond coroutine) and measure RSS and spawn rate. Requires the timer wheel from M1 time work.
acceptance_criteria: RSS < 2.5 GB and spawn >= 1M/s on one lane on the reference machine; recorded in bench/results.

title: from_thread.run/run_sync and Portal
description: from_thread.run(async_fn) and run_sync(fn) from worker threads block until done on a Python lane; on a lane thread raise RuntimeError immediately. Portal: submit -> concurrent.futures.Future, work runs in a portal-owned child scope, close() cancels outstanding work. Runtime.portal().
acceptance_criteria: Tests: round trip from to_thread worker; lane-thread call raises RuntimeError; portal from a plain threading.Thread; close cancels pending work.

title: Interpreter finalization safety
description: atexit hook shuts down any running runtime; lanes and blocking workers stop touching Python once Py_IsFinalizing(); pending deferred decrefs are leaked, not executed.
acceptance_criteria: Test: process exiting with a runtime running in a daemon thread exits cleanly (no crash) across 100 runs.

title: Fork handling: warn before, poison runtime in child
description: os.register_at_fork: before -> RuntimeWarning if a runtime is running; after_in_child -> mark all runtimes poisoned so any use raises RuntimeClosed('runtime does not survive fork()'); fresh runtime creatable in the child.
acceptance_criteria: Tests (Unix): fork inside run warns; child using inherited runtime raises RuntimeClosed; child can porto.run a new main.

title: Async generator hooks per lane
description: sys.set_asyncgen_hooks(firstiter, finalizer) installed per lane thread on first run; firstiter registers agen in lane weak set; finalizer spawns agen.aclose() into the root scope with shield and 5 s deadline; all tracked agens closed at shutdown before lanes stop.
acceptance_criteria: Test: abandoned async generator's finally runs (with await) during run and at shutdown.

title: Debug mode: coroutine origin, spawn site, never-awaited traps
description: debug=True (or PORTO_DEBUG=1, -X dev): set_coroutine_origin_tracking_depth(8), spawn site captured (extract_stack limit 10, compact string) and appended as note 'task spawned at ...' on unhandled task exceptions, RuntimeWarning on dealloc of a never-awaited trap.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for each of the three behaviours; zero overhead when debug=False (benchmark unchanged).

title: External: what porto needs from oxiform
description: OX-1..OX-10 land in github.com/m4nd0r4s/oxiform. These issues track them so Douro tasks can depend on them; the work itself happens in the oxiform repo.
acceptance_criteria: An oxiform release with OX-1..OX-5 (and OX-6) published; Douro pins it.

title: M8 — Hardening to 1.0
description: Fuzzing campaigns, soak, PGO, wheel matrix, security review, API freeze, io_uring and IOCP backends, 1.0 release.
acceptance_criteria: S1-S7 gates pass; porto and douro 1.0.0 published.

title: M7 — Douro complete
description: WebSockets, SSE, multipart, files, compression, Rust layers, Python middleware, OpenAPI and docs, supervisor and CLI, reload, ASGI mount.
acceptance_criteria: h2spec and Autobahn pass; graceful-shutdown zero-loss test; docs complete.

title: M6 — Douro core
description: Router, oxiform integration, HandlerPlan, DI, responses, HTTP/1.1 and h2 server, limits, errors, test client.
acceptance_criteria: HTTP gates (53 §4) on JSON, path-param and POST.

title: M5 — Observability and deterministic testing
description: inspect, watchdog, metrics, console TUI, OpenTelemetry; porto-sim, simulated network, pytest plugin, explore.
acceptance_criteria: S4: deterministic mode reproduces 100% of seeded failures across 1000 reruns; console demo.

title: M4 — asyncio and AnyIO compatibility
description: asyncio facade loop (transports, subprocess, signals), bridging, auto-hosting, native AnyIO backend, sniffio.
acceptance_criteria: S2: asyncpg, redis.asyncio, httpx and aiohttp suites pass >= 95% under porto.

title: Specify LayerVTable in douro-core layer_abi.rs
description: §35 §3 says the custom Rust layer vtable is specified in douro-core/src/layer_abi.rs in M8 while the roadmap puts 'layer ABI' in M9. Write the #[repr(C)] LayerVTable definition and versioning notes (mirroring porto-abi B.3) without exporting the _LAYER_ABI_V1 capsule, so 1.0 does not paint the layer ABI into a corner; implementation is m9-layer-abi.
acceptance_criteria: layer_abi.rs compiles with the vtable and doc comments; reviewed against porto-abi rules; no public capsule exported.

title: douro bench built-in load generator
description: douro bench app /path: Rust h1/h2 load generator on Porto printing a latency histogram.
acceptance_criteria: Runs against a sample app and prints p50/p99/p999 and RPS.

title: App(unknown="forbid") for request bodies
description: Expose App(unknown="forbid") to reject unknown keys in request bodies globally using the oxiform per-call override.
acceptance_criteria: Test: unknown key in body -> 422 when enabled, ignored by default.

title: Response content negotiation: msgpack and YAML
description: Honor Accept: application/msgpack and application/yaml by encoding with the matching ox.<format> encoder against the declared type; JSON default; 406 not used (fallback to JSON).
acceptance_criteria: Negotiation tests per format with q-values.

title: OX-10: key-string cache for dict keys
description: oxiform should intern/cache dict key strings in the Python sink instead of allocating a new str per key, reducing allocation on untyped dict bodies.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform microbenchmark shows fewer allocations and no regression on typed models.

title: OX-8: single-document tape via OX-1
description: oxiform should validate a single document into a tape without the interpreter attached and materialize Python objects later, so Douro can reject 422s on a Rust lane and relieve the GIL. Optional perf feature.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform API validates on a non-Python thread and materializes on the Python thread; benchmark shows 422 rejections without attaching the interpreter.

title: Deterministic mode for pure-Rust users (#[porto::test(seed)])
description: Expose porto-sim to Rust: `Builder::deterministic(seed)`, `#[porto::test(seed = .., seeds = N)]`, sim network handle and virtual-clock control. Not spelled out in the spec; proposed so porto-sim (a no-Python crate) is usable by the `porto` crate.
acceptance_criteria: Rust test using #[porto::test(seeds = 100)] runs 100 seeds and prints the failing seed; same-seed trace identical across reruns.

title: Rust tracing spans for runtime internals (feature `tracing`)
description: Instrument scheduler, driver, timers and scope transitions with `tracing` spans/events behind cargo feature `tracing` (off in release wheels).
acceptance_criteria: Feature-on build emits spans in a tracing-subscriber test; feature-off build has no tracing dependency (cargo tree check).

title: Propose anyio.backends entry-point group upstream
description: Open an AnyIO issue/PR proposing an `anyio.backends` entry-point group so third-party backends can register without touching private internals. Also file the CPython idea for a cheap foreign current-task hook. Track status in 55.
acceptance_criteria: Upstream issue/PR links recorded in 55-risks-open-questions.md.

title: io_uring completion fast paths for net and fs
description: Internal completion paths in porto-net/porto-fs only: multishot accept, recv into provided buffer rings (IORING_REGISTER_PBUF_RING) for TcpStream reads into pooled Buffers, send with registered buffers for Buffer writes, openat/read/write/statx for porto-fs. ABI users keep readiness semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Net/fs suites green; TCP echo benchmark with io_uring >= epoll result (no regression) on the reference machine; fs read_bytes avoids the blocking pool (counter).

title: Optional hickory async resolver (feature 'hickory')
description: porto.net.Resolver.hickory(...) behind cargo feature 'hickory': async DNS on the Porto driver with real TTLs, pluggable into connect_tcp/resolve.
acceptance_criteria: Tests against a local UDP DNS stub: TTL respected; feature off -> AttributeError/ImportError with clear message.

title: Debug detection of threading.local use across migration
description: In debug mode wrap threading.local.__getattribute__ to mark tasks that touched thread-locals; warn when such a task migrates lanes. Best effort, debug only. Plus doc section on pin=True / python_steal='off'.
acceptance_criteria: Test: debug mode warns when a task using threading.local is stolen; no wrapper installed when debug=False.

title: Open question: CPython hook for foreign current-task registration
description: Propose a CPython asyncio hook letting foreign task implementations register a current task cheaply (asyncio.current_task, introspection tools). Current default: the compat facade handles it; the upstream proposal is optional and not depended on.
acceptance_criteria: Decision on whether to file a CPython discussion/PEP recorded; link if filed.

title: Open question: upstream AnyIO backend registry proposal
description: Propose an anyio.backends entry-point group upstream so the Porto backend no longer injects into AnyIO's private cache. Current default: injection behind a version gate, with the proposal pursued in parallel and nothing depending on its acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal filed upstream and linked; switch to the entry point if merged.

title: Open question: Windows IoRing backend
description: A Windows IoRing backend analogous to io_uring. Current default: no; Windows uses IOCP via mio's readiness emulation.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded as final for v1 (NG7).

title: Open question: exposing Douro over ASGI
description: Exposing a Douro app as an ASGI callable for serverless and platform compatibility. Current default: no; it would lose the one-crossing architecture. Use douro run.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded; revisit only on concrete platform demand.

title: Open question: native Rust DB drivers on Porto
description: A Postgres wire-protocol driver in Rust on Porto that materializes rows directly into oxiform models would be the next 2x for DB-bound Douro endpoints. Current default: candidate separate project after 1.0, not part of porto/douro.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded after 1.0 (separate repo or not pursued).

title: Open question: subinterpreters (PEP 734) as lanes on GIL builds
description: Subinterpreter-per-lane for parallelism without free-threading, with copy-based channels across interpreters. Current default: not in v1 (NG2); research item that could become an 'isolated lanes' mode in v2.
acceptance_criteria: Decided from the m9-subinterpreter-research report.

title: Open question: select-like API
description: Whether to add porto.select(*branches) after v1. Current default: none; users compose a scope of competing tasks plus scope.cancel(), or rx.recv_many, because select over partially completed operations is a main source of lost-message bugs in Tokio.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded after 1.0 user feedback; m9-select proceeds or closes.

title: Open question: porto.run lanes="auto" on free-threaded builds
description: Should porto.run default to lanes="auto" on free-threaded builds? Current default: no, 1 lane (ADR-025; Douro alone defaults to auto). Revisit when CPython announces Phase III of free-threading.
acceptance_criteria: Revisited at the Phase III announcement; ADR-025 updated or reaffirmed.

title: Research: subinterpreters (PEP 734) as isolated lanes
description: Prototype an 'isolated lanes' mode on GIL builds where each extra lane hosts a subinterpreter with its own GIL, channels copy across interpreters, and the runtime remains single-owner. Measure throughput vs processes and vs 3.14t lanes, and list blocking issues (extension module support, cross-interpreter object costs).
acceptance_criteria: Written report with benchmarks and a go/no-go recommendation for v2 feeding dec-subinterpreter-lanes.

title: Custom Rust layer ABI (_LAYER_ABI_V1 capsule)
description: Export the LayerVTable through the douro._native._LAYER_ABI_V1 capsule and a douro-abi crate so a third-party Rust crate can register layers configured from Python by name. Versioning follows porto-abi B.3; an example layer crate in examples/ is tested in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Example layer wheel registers, runs in the pre-route and route positions, and an ABI-mismatch is refused with a clear error.

title: FastAPI to Douro codemod
description: douro migrate (libcst-based) rewriting the §41 §3 mapping: FastAPI() to douro.App(), APIRouter to Router, param markers, HTTPException to HTTPError, BackgroundTasks to Background, middleware decorator, response classes, TestClient. Untranslatable constructs get a TODO comment and a report line.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture FastAPI apps convert, type-check under pyright and pass their ported tests; the report lists every manual step.

title: porto.select API (if dec-select-api accepts it)
description: If the decision lands on providing it, implement porto.select(*branches) restricted to cancel-safe operations (recv, Event.wait, sleep, task join) so a losing branch never consumes a message, with typed branch results. Otherwise close in favour of documented scope+cancel and recv_many patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Loom/deterministic tests show no lost messages when branches race; pyright infers the result union; or the issue closes with the pattern docs.

title: WebSockets over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT)
description: Enable SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL and accept extended CONNECT with :protocol = websocket on h2 connections, mapping the stream to the same WebSocket API used over h1. Autobahn run over h2 where tooling allows.
acceptance_criteria: A WS client over h2 (e.g. a test client using h2 + extended CONNECT) completes echo and close handshakes; existing h1 WS tests run unchanged on the h2 path.

title: HTTP/3 over quinn with Alt-Svc advertisement
description: QUIC via quinn with UDP I/O through the porto ABI (io_register on a UDP socket) and h3 on top, producing the same RequestHead + body stream so the pipeline from the router onward is unchanged. Advertise via Alt-Svc; rustls config shared with h1/h2. Likely several PRs (UDP runtime adapter, h3 glue, config/limits).
acceptance_criteria: curl --http3 and an h3 client test pass against douro run; Alt-Svc emitted when enabled; limits from §40 apply to h3 requests.

title: oxiform pydantic shim (oxiform 1.2)
description: Tracking: oxiform 1.2 is expected to ship a pydantic shim. When available, Douro removes its own __pydantic_validator__ adapter (m6-pydantic-adapter) and routes pydantic models through oxiform.
acceptance_criteria: oxiform release with shim; Douro pydantic test suite passes with the adapter removed.

title: M9+ — Post-1.0
description: HTTP/3 (quinn), RFC 8441 WebSockets over h2, select, FastAPI codemod, layer ABI, subinterpreter research.
acceptance_criteria: Each item ships or is decided against.
